# CharAI: full documentation

> CharAI is an open-source (Apache 2.0) 2D character animation engine and agent skill. An AI agent, or a person, draws any human as a small data file and directs it with a short `.char` script; the engine supplies skeleton, motion, physics, moods, lip sync and speech, two-character contact and props. Characters only (the host supplies scenery), side view only in this release, no runtime dependencies, one script file `dist/char.js`. Exports MP4, transparent WebM and ProRes, PNG sequence and animated SVG. Version 0.1.0.

Generated by `node tools/llms.cjs`. Files in reading order; each begins with a separator line.

# CharAI: 2D character animation engine and AI agent skill

CharAI is an open-source 2D character animation engine and agent skill (a Claude Code skill, usable by any agent that can read a skill file and run Node). It is for people and AI agents who want text to animation for human characters: the agent draws any human as a small data file (a skeletal rig skin, SVG paths), directs it with a short `.char` script, and CharAI supplies motion, physics, moods, lip sync and speech, two-character contact and props. Characters only, side view only. Every frame is a pure function of time (`seek(t)`), so any tool with a clock can drive it.

No runtime dependencies: one script file, `dist/char.js`, and a `<char-stage>` web component. Export MP4, transparent WebM and ProRes, PNG sequence, or animated SVG. Scenery is not drawn; the host supplies it.

## The .char script

A film is plain text. This one is complete:

```
film "Hello" 6s
actor Kai = skin kai at 160
0.0 Kai: walk(to=700), face(happy)
2.0 Kai: say("Nice to meet you.", for=2)
```

Each line is a time, an actor and calls such as `walk`, `face`, `say`, `hug`. More single-file examples: [`examples/`](examples/). Full syntax: [`docs/AUTHORING.md`](docs/AUTHORING.md).

## Works with

- **Claude Code and Claude models.** Built with them (see the FAQ). Only Claude models have been tried; any agent that can read a skill file and run Node can use it.
- **Hosts.** Plain HTML pages: tested (`examples/host.html`, `examples/page.html`). Remotion, HyperFrames and GSAP: snippets in [`docs/HOSTS.md`](docs/HOSTS.md), not yet tested.
- **Style libraries** such as Lemo-Opuscar: meant as a character layer beside them. There is no integration code.

## Install as an agent skill

Copy or clone this repository into the agent's skills folder; for Claude Code that is `.claude/skills/charai/`. The agent then reads [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md), which sends it to one document for each of three jobs: draw a character ([`docs/CHARACTER.md`](docs/CHARACTER.md)), write a film ([`docs/AUTHORING.md`](docs/AUTHORING.md)), add an action ([`docs/ACTIONS.md`](docs/ACTIONS.md)).

## Quick start

Needs Node 18 or newer. For pictures and video, also Chrome or Edge, `npm install` once (`puppeteer-core`), and ffmpeg on the PATH for MP4.

```
node --test tests/*.cjs                       # the test suite
node tools/check.cjs films/demo               # check a film; writes films/demo/index.html
node tools/render.cjs films/demo demo.mp4     # an MP4
```

A character is a skin file: numbers on top of the `mannequin` skin plus a few SVG paths ([`docs/CHARACTER.md`](docs/CHARACTER.md)).

## Evidence in short

Figures from [`docs/EVIDENCE.md`](docs/EVIDENCE.md); each case was run once.

- A character skin: 1.3 to 2.2 KB, about 41,800 tokens and about 40 s each (6 characters, Claude Sonnet).
- An action: about 8,200 tokens and 9 s each (36 actions, all passed the checker).
- A 20 s scene, two characters, moods, 3 own actions: 98,844 tokens, 2.4 minutes.
- Two 30 s episodes against the style-library workflow, both on Sonnet: 425,057 tokens against 667,202, 25 minutes against 74.
- **Where CharAI lost:** a 30 s silhouette film on Opus cost 391,611 tokens and 35.7 minutes against 318,987 and 24.7, and the other film looked better. Not re-run.

## FAQ

**What is CharAI?**
CharAI is an open-source 2D character animation engine and agent skill. An AI agent or a person draws any human as a small skin data file and directs it with a short `.char` script; the engine supplies skeleton, motion, physics, moods, lip sync, two-character contact and props.

**How do I animate a character with Claude Code?**
Put this repository in `.claude/skills/charai/` and ask Claude Code to draw a character or write a film. It reads `SKILL.md`, follows the document for the job, then loops: write, run the check (`node tools/check.cjs films/x`), look at the picture, fix.

**Does it work with HyperFrames, Remotion or GSAP?**
The frame is a pure function of time (`seek(t)`), the contract those timelines use, and `docs/HOSTS.md` has a snippet for each. Those three snippets are untested; HyperFrames is "snippet provided, not yet tested". Two plain-HTML host examples in `examples/` are tested.

**How does it compare with Lemo-Opuscar?**
Lemo-Opuscar is a style library for code-made films. On two 30 s episodes on Sonnet, CharAI used 425,057 tokens against 667,202; on a 30 s silhouette film on Opus it lost, at 391,611 against 318,987, and looked worse. These are single runs, and CharAI is meant to complement style libraries as their character layer.

**Which models built it?**
It was built with Claude Code. Claude Fable 5.2 was architect and reviewer, Claude Opus 5.5 wrote the engine code, and Claude Sonnet wrote characters, actions, scenes, tools and packaging from the documents alone. Only Claude models have been tried.

**What does it cost in tokens?**
Claude Sonnet wrote a character in about 41,800 tokens, an action in about 8,200, and a 20 s two-character scene in 98,844. Each figure is one run; see `docs/EVIDENCE.md`.

**What can't it do?**
Side view only (no three-quarter or front view), flat cartoon styles, no scenery, no 3D, simple hands, and spring physics for hair and cloth rather than simulation. Lip sync matches the speech but is not polished. Known faults are in `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`.

**Does it need an artist or motion capture?**
No. The agent writes a skin as numbers plus a few SVG paths, and motion comes from the engine's actions, which are a few key poses each. There is no library of ready-made characters; a few worked examples are in `skins/`.

**What licence is it under?**
Apache License 2.0; see `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`. It has no runtime dependencies.

**How do I add a new action?**
Write a small file of key poses in body terms, register it in `CharActions`, and check it with `node tools/actioncheck.cjs actions/x.js`. See it with `node tools/action.cjs x out.png`. The format is in `docs/ACTIONS.md`.

## Limits and status

Known faults: [`docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`](docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md). Agents wrote all of the code; no person has reviewed it line by line yet. Next: three-quarter and front views.

Licence: Apache 2.0, [`LICENSE`](LICENSE), [`NOTICE`](NOTICE).

---
name: charai
description: CharAI is a 2D character animation engine and agent skill that draws and animates side-view cartoon people with a deterministic engine (seek(t) gives the same frame in any order). Use it to design a character as a data file, write a short animated film as a text .char script (walk, run, jump, emotions, speech with lip sync, hugs, props), add a new action, export video or animated SVG, or place animated characters over another tool's scenery. Characters only; no scenery, no 3D, side view only.
---

# CharAI: where to start

You draw the character; CharAI moves it. Run everything from this folder with Node. Read the document for
your job, then loop: write, check, look at the picture, fix.

| Job | Read | Check and look |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draw a character (a skin file: numbers plus a few SVG paths) | `docs/CHARACTER.md`, then `docs/RIG.md` for every field | `node tools/skincheck.cjs skins/x.js`, `node tools/cast.cjs skins/x.js x.png` |
| Write a film (a `film.char` script: actors, actions, camera, captions) | `docs/AUTHORING.md` | `node tools/check.cjs films/x`, `node tools/sheet.cjs films/x` |
| Add an action (a few key poses in a small file) | `docs/ACTIONS.md` | `node tools/actioncheck.cjs actions/x.js`, `node tools/action.cjs x out.png` |

## Also

- **Speech and faces**: `docs/SPEECH.md`. `say("text", for=2)` lip-syncs from text alone; a timing track
  from a voice tool makes it tighter. `tools/say.cjs` shows the mouth shapes.
- **Voices**: `docs/VOICE-WINDOWS.md` makes a voice track on Windows; `node tools/render.cjs films/x out.mp4 --audio=voice.wav`
  adds the sound.
- **Two characters** (handshake, hug, shove, hand over): `docs/PAIRS.md`.
- **Props** (pick up, carry, throw, sit on, lean on): `docs/PROPS.md`; props in pairs are in `docs/PAIRS.md`.
- **Embed in another tool** (web component `<char-stage>`, `Char.mount`, page-owned clock, transparent
  PNG, WebM or ProRes export): `docs/HOSTS.md`. Build the bundle with `npm run build`.

## Rules that save time

- Start a skin by extending `mannequin` and setting numbers; draw only the head, hair, clothes and
  accessories. Never copy helper code from another skin; a skin is plain data.
- A film needs no scenery line. The host paints the scenery; keep its ground line at the script's `ground=`.
- Never say it is done before the check passes and you have looked at the picture.
- `npm install` is only for the screenshot and render tools.

Limits: side view only, flat cartoon styles, believable (not simulated) physics, simple hands. See
`README.md` and `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`.

# AGENTS.md

CharAI is a 2D character animation engine and agent skill. You draw a human as a small skin file, direct it with a `.char` script, and the engine supplies skeleton, motion, physics, lip sync and contact. Characters only, side view only. Apache 2.0, no runtime dependencies. Start with `SKILL.md`.

## Three jobs

| Job | Read first |
| --- | --- |
| Draw a character (skin file) | `docs/CHARACTER.md`, then `docs/RIG.md` |
| Write a film (`.char` script) | `docs/AUTHORING.md` |
| Add an action | `docs/ACTIONS.md` |

Speech `docs/SPEECH.md`; two characters `docs/PAIRS.md`; props `docs/PROPS.md`; other tools `docs/HOSTS.md`.

## Commands

```
node --test tests/*.cjs                 # test suite
node tools/skincheck.cjs skins/x.js     # check a skin
node tools/actioncheck.cjs actions/x.js # check an action
node tools/check.cjs films/x            # check a film
node tools/sheet.cjs films/x            # contact sheet to look at
npm run build                           # rebuild dist/char.js after editing src/
npm run llms                            # regenerate llms.txt and llms-full.txt
```

Screenshot and render tools need `npm install` (puppeteer-core); do not run it otherwise.

## Rules

- Run the check and the tests before saying a job is done.
- Look at the picture (cast sheet, contact sheet) before claiming it looks right.
- Side view only; do not draw scenery; do not claim untested host support.
- A skin is plain data; extend `mannequin`, never copy helper code.


========================================
FILE: docs/CHARACTER.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/CHARACTER.md
========================================

# CHARACTER.md: draw a character for CharAI

You write ONE file, a **skin**: numbers for the body and SVG paths for what is distinctive (head,
hair, clothes, accessories). CharAI supplies skeleton, motion and the physics of hair and cloth.
Full fields and recipes: `docs/RIG.md`. Follow this page in order.

## Commands

```
node tools/skincheck.cjs skins/mia.js          # rules check; fix every ERROR it prints
node tools/cast.cjs skins/mia.js mia.png       # picture: standing, walk, run, jump, wave, sit
```

Check after every edit; cast and LOOK at the whole picture after every step. Both accept
`films/<film>/skins/mia.js`.

## Units and directions

- One unit = one head height, for every length and path coordinate. Not pixels.
- Side view, **facing right**: +x is forward (face, toes, belly), **-x is the back** (ponytail,
  backpack, hood), **+y is up**.
- Head, hair: origin at the top of the neck, the head
  spans y = 0 (chin) to 1 (crown), x from -0.5 (back of skull) to +0.5 (nose). The generated face:
  eye centre (0.3, 0.55), brow (0.3, 0.68), mouth (0.38, 0.24), ear (-0.06, 0.5). Torso: origin at the hip line, y up to the neck base; height 0.4 at 2.2 heads, 0.84 at 3,
  1.8 at 5, 2.6 at 7, 2.9 at 8.

## The skin file

File name, `name` and key are the same word.

```js
(function (g) {
  (g.CharSkins = g.CharSkins || {}).mia = { name: 'mia', extends: 'mannequin',
    build:   { heads: 5.5 },
    motion:  { weight: 0.3, energy: 0.6 },
    palette: { skin: '#d9a07a', hair: '#2b1d16', suit: '#2f6f6a' },
    parts:   { },
    chains:  { } };
})(typeof self !== 'undefined' ? self : this);
```

`extends: 'mannequin'` gives a complete person from your numbers; `parts` draw ON TOP of it.

## The loop

1. Copy the template. Check, cast, look.
2. Set `build` and `motion` (next section). Check, cast, look. Do not draw anything until the
   body shape, stride and stoop suit the person.
3. Palette. `skin`, `hair`, `shoe` recolour the body. **Set `suit` to the colour of the main
   garment (or the skin)**: the body wears a grey suit that shows at the neck, shoulders and hips
   wherever clothes leave a gap. Every `fill` must be a palette name or a literal `'#rrggbb'`.
   `fooShade` is made automatically, but only if `foo` exists.
4. Head, only if the generated one is wrong. 5. Hair. 6. Garments, one at a time, then
   accessories. Check, cast, look after each.
7. Final look at all SIX poses (standing, walk, run, jump, wave, sit).

Look for: grey at neck, shoulders or hips (set `suit`); hair or a hat floating off the head; a
garment poking past a limb; a long coat as a torso cover (use a skirt); an invisible chain (wrong
`layer`); a hem swallowing the feet; magenta (unknown colour).

## Choosing numbers

`build.heads` is height in heads; everything else defaults from it, so set only what differs.
Chest, shoulders, waist, hips are side-view DEPTH. Long neck: `neckLength` 0-1.2 (the torso shortens to keep the height). Ranges: `arm` 0.05-0.3, `leg` 0.1-0.45, depths 0.35-1.3, `belly` 0-0.7, `heads` 2.2-8, `muscle` 0-1 (RIG.md section 4).

| Person | build | motion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| toddler | `{ heads: 2.3 }` | `{ age: 'baby', energy: 0.8, weight: 0.2 }` |
| teen | `{ heads: 6.2 }` | `{ energy: 0.7 }` |
| heavy adult | `{ heads: 5.6, belly: 0.55, chest: 1.05, waist: 1.0, hips: 0.98, seat: 0.1, arm: 0.17, leg: 0.3 }` | `{ weight: 0.9, energy: 0.35 }` |
| elder | `{ heads: 6.6, belly: 0.14, arm: 0.11, leg: 0.19 }` | `{ age: 'elder', posture: 0.7, energy: 0.3 }` |
| tall thin adult | `{ heads: 8, chest: 0.72, waist: 0.52, hips: 0.78, arm: 0.1, leg: 0.16 }` | `{ weight: 0.1, energy: 0.5 }` |

A child is `{ heads: 3.5 }`, `age: 'child'`; an athlete `{ heads: 7.4, muscle: 1 }`. `weight` 0 light to 1 heavy; `energy` 0 tired to 1
lively; `age` baby, child, adult, elder; `posture` -1 proud to 1 stooped.

## Head, face and hair cap

The generated head has a hair cap in `palette.hair`:
- **Bald or your own hair shape:** `build: { heads: 6, hide: ['hair'] }` removes only the cap
  (`hide: ['head']` removes the whole head, face included). Then draw `parts.hair`. Always hide
  the cap under a hat, or it shows below the brim.
- **Different skull:** `parts.head` replaces the generated head: skin shape, then the face swaps:

```js
head: [ { d: 'M-0.42 0.5C-0.42 0.15 -0.2 0 0.1 0C0.4 0 0.5 0.2 0.5 0.5C0.5 0.85 0.3 1 0 1C-0.3 1 -0.42 0.85 -0.42 0.5Z', fill: 'skin' },
        { swap: 'brow' }, { swap: 'eye' }, { swap: 'mouth' } ],
```

Your own eyes and mouths (names in RIG.md section 8; giving `eye` keeps the generated mouth and
brows; `look: 1` follows the gaze). Brows (`neutral up down worried`) are strokes at y 0.65-0.75,
just above the eye, e.g. `brow: { neutral: { d: 'M0.22 0.67Q0.28 0.7 0.36 0.68', stroke: 'brow', w: 0.035 } }`:

```js
swaps: { eye: { open: [{ d: 'M0.24 0.55A0.05 0.07 0 1 0 0.34 0.55A0.05 0.07 0 1 0 0.24 0.55Z', fill: 'eye', look: 1 }],
                closed: { d: 'M0.24 0.56Q0.29 0.52 0.34 0.56', stroke: 'eye', w: 0.022 } } }
```

**A speaking face.** If you draw your own head, also give `swaps.mouth`, or it talks with the
generated mouth, which may not fit your face. Minimum: `open` and `closed`. Better: add
the mood mouths (`neutral smile sad o grit worried`). Best: the nine speech mouths `rest mbp ah ee oh
oo fv l wq`; missing ones fall back. Centre every mouth near (0.38, 0.24).
A beard or moustache must be its own path in `parts.head` or `parts.hair`, below y 0.32 (not
merged with the hair), so it moves with the jaw. Speech: `docs/SPEECH.md`.

A line is `{ d, stroke, w: 0.03 }`.

## Hair that moves

Static hair: a filled head-frame path in `parts.hair` (over the head) or `parts.hairBack` (behind).
Swinging hair is a **chain**:

```js
chains: { pony: { bone: 'head', at: [-0.45, 0.8], rest: 190, seg: [0.25, 0.22],
  width: [0.15, 0.13, 0.04], fill: 'hair', layer: 'back', stiff: 0.35 } }
```

`bone` head, neck, torso, pelvis; `at` anchor in that frame; `rest` degrees (0 forward, 90 up,
180 back, 270 down); `seg` lengths; `width` has ONE MORE number than `seg`; `stiff` 0 loose to 1
rigid. **`layer`**: `back` only for things hanging out behind the body (ponytail, cape,
backpack); `head` for things on the face or head (earring, fringe); `torso` for things lying on
the back or chest (braid, pendant). A scarf: bone `neck`, `stiff` 0.15. Backpack: RIG.md section 11.

## Clothes

Garments fit any body. Fractions run 0 to 1 along the part.

| Garment | Write |
| --- | --- |
| T-shirt or top | `torso: { cover: true, loose: 0.03, fill: 'shirt' }` and `arm: { cover: [0, 0.3], flat: 'end', fill: 'shirt' }` |
| long sleeves | `arm: { cover: [0, 0.95], loose: 0.03, fill: 'coat' }` |
| shorts / trousers | `leg: { cover: [0, 0.35], fill: 'jeans' }` / `leg: { cover: [0, 1], loose: 0.02, fill: 'jeans' }` |
| boots | `leg: { cover: [0.8, 1.02], loose: 0.03, flat: 'start', fill: 'boot' }` |
| skirt, dress, long coat, tunic, long apron | `skirt: { skirt: true, length: 0.5, flare: 0.2, fill: 'dress' }` plus a bodice `torso: { cover: [0.3, 1.1], fill: 'dress' }` |
| cardigan over a shirt | a list: `torso: [{ cover: true, fill: 'shirt' }, { cover: true, loose: 0.04, fill: 'coat' }]` (later covers lie on earlier ones) |

A torso cover stops at the hip line. **Anything that hangs lower is a `skirt`**, never a long
torso cover, because only the skirt follows the legs when she runs or sits. `length` 0 hips, 0.5
knee, 1 ankle; full long dress `flare` 0.25-0.35; `hem: { fill, w: 0.08 }` adds a trim; `shade` is
a colour name. A part may be a list, drawn in order.

- Hat, glasses, hood, pocket, apron, earrings, backpack: RIG.md section 11.
- Cane: `holdNear: { use: 'cane', length: 2.6, d: 'M-0.025 0.05L0.025 0.05L0.025 -2.6L-0.025 -2.6Z', fill: 'wood' }`
  (`length` about 0.45 x heads); the engine plants it in step with the walk. A bag that hangs
  straight: `holdFar: { upright: true, ... }`. Both keys only work in `holdNear`/`holdFar`.

## Rules

1. `swap` only in `parts.head`; `tube` only in `arm`, `leg`; `cap` only in `upperArm`, `foreArm`,
   `thigh`, `shin`; garments use `cover` or `skirt`.
2. Change one thing, check, look. Never write the whole character before the first cast.
3. Fix a body problem with `build` or `motion`, not with clothes. Leave `outline` (max 0.04),
   `springs`, `grip`, `handZ` alone.

Done: `OK: 0 errors, 0 warnings` and six poses of one whole person. Actions and moods are in
`docs/ACTIONS.md`.


========================================
FILE: docs/RIG.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/RIG.md
========================================

# RIG.md: the CharAI skin contract

A **skin** is one JavaScript file of plain data that tells CharAI what a character looks
like. CharAI owns the skeleton and all motion; the skin only says how big the body is, what
it is like to move, and what to draw on each bone. This file is the complete reference: every
field, which ones are required, and every default.

## 1. The file

```js
// skins/<name>.js   (or films/<film>/skins/<name>.js, which wins for that film)
(function (g) {
  (g.CharSkins = g.CharSkins || {}).NAME = { name: 'NAME', /* fields below */ };
})(typeof self !== 'undefined' ? self : this);
```

`name` must equal the file name and the key. A film uses it with
`actor Mia = skin NAME at 400 [scale=1]`.

## 2. Units and frames

- **Unit: head heights.** 1 = the height of the head. All lengths, radii and path coordinates
  are in head heights; the stage converts (px per head = the stage `scale` times the actor's
  `scale=`; default 68 px).
- **Side view, facing right.** +x is forward (the way the character faces), **+y is up**,
  angles are degrees counter-clockwise from +x. Draw everything facing right; the engine
  mirrors it.
- **Frames (`parent` and `pivot`).** Every part is drawn in the frame of the bone it is
  attached to; the part's key names that bone (its parent), the frame origin is the pivot,
  and the frame turns with the bone (its rotation):

| Part key | Origin (pivot) | Axes, scale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `head`, `hair`, `hairBack` | top of the neck (the jaw hinge) | x forward, y up; the head spans y = 0..1 |
| `neck` | base of the neck | x forward, y up |
| `torso` | the pelvis (hip joint level) | x forward, y up; the torso runs y = 0..`proportions.torso`. The engine bends and squashes this frame (spine), so draw closed shapes |
| `pelvis` | the pelvis | x forward, y up |
| `arm`, `leg` | whole limb | a tube through shoulder-elbow-wrist or hip-knee-ankle (see 5) |
| `upperArm`, `foreArm`, `thigh`, `shin` | the upper joint | x runs 0..1 along the bone, y across it in head units times bone length |
| `foot` | the ankle | x along the sole (forward), y up; the sole is at y = -`ankleHeight` |
| hand swaps, `hand`, `holdNear`, `holdFar` | the wrist | x along the fingers, +y = thumb side |

**Which way is the back.** -x is always the back: a backpack, a ponytail or a hood hangs at
negative x; the face, toes and belly are at positive x.

**Frame sizes for a generated body** (`build` only; read them off this table or from
`proportions` if you set it):

| heads | torso height | shoulder below torso top | thigh | shin | ankle height | upper arm | forearm | hand | foot | chest depth | hip depth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2.2 | 0.40 | 0.10 | 0.32 | 0.30 | 0.08 | 0.22 | 0.20 | 0.20 | 0.42 | 0.52 | 0.52 |
| 3 | 0.84 | 0.13 | 0.48 | 0.44 | 0.10 | 0.33 | 0.29 | 0.26 | 0.51 | 0.58 | 0.57 |
| 4 | 1.36 | 0.16 | 0.70 | 0.64 | 0.12 | 0.49 | 0.43 | 0.33 | 0.62 | 0.65 | 0.63 |
| 5 | 1.82 | 0.20 | 0.94 | 0.87 | 0.15 | 0.66 | 0.59 | 0.40 | 0.74 | 0.73 | 0.68 |
| 6 | 2.23 | 0.23 | 1.22 | 1.12 | 0.17 | 0.86 | 0.76 | 0.48 | 0.85 | 0.80 | 0.74 |
| 7 | 2.59 | 0.27 | 1.51 | 1.40 | 0.20 | 1.07 | 0.95 | 0.55 | 0.97 | 0.88 | 0.80 |
| 8 | 2.90 | 0.30 | 1.84 | 1.70 | 0.22 | 1.30 | 1.16 | 0.62 | 1.08 | 0.95 | 0.86 |

The torso frame runs from y = 0 (hip line) to y = torso height (base of the neck); its front edge
is at about +depth/2 and its back at -depth/2 (plus `belly` at the front around 0.36 of the
height, `seat` at the back near 0). A cover's `[from, to]` uses fractions of this height.

**The generated head** (head frame, W = `build.headWidth`): eye centre (0.3 W, 0.55), brow just
above it (0.3 W, 0.68), mouth (0.38 W, 0.24), ear centre (-0.06 W, 0.5), jaw line from the chin
(0.14 W, 0.02) to (0.32 W, 0.12), nose tip (0.52 W, 0.47), top of the skull y = 1.02, back of the
skull x = -0.53 W. The hair cap covers the top and back, from (-0.48 W, 0.66) over the crown to
(0.43 W, 0.76). A hat sits on y = 0.95-1.05; glasses at the eye height.

## 3. Top-level fields

| Field | Required | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | | the skin's name |
| `extends` | no | | name of a skin to start from; this skin's keys replace or (for `palette`, `proportions`, `build`, `motion`, `parts`, `swaps`, `chains`, `springs`) merge into its keys. `extends: 'mannequin'` is the normal start |
| `build` | no (yes for a generated body) | see 4 | the body from numbers. With `build`, the engine draws a whole body and the skin adds to it |
| `motion` | no | `{ weight: 0.3, energy: 0.5, age: 'adult', posture: 0 }` | how the body moves (see 6) |
| `proportions` | no | from `build.heads`, else the default figure (about 3.4 heads) | bone lengths (see 4) |
| `headTop` | no | 1.04 | top of the hair above the head origin (height, framing) |
| `outline` | no | 0.03 with `build`, else 0 | ink line width in head units (0 = flat; 0.04 = bold) |
| `farShade` | no | 0.85 | the far arm and leg are darkened by this factor |
| `palette` | no | the mannequin's | colour names to `#rrggbb` (see 7) |
| `parts` | no | the generated body | what to draw on each bone (see 5) |
| `swaps` | no | generated faces and hands | drawings that change with the action or mood (see 8) |
| `chains` | no | | spring chains: hair locks, scarf tails, backpacks, hems (see 9) |
| `springs` | no | `{ arms: 1, head: 1, torso: 1 }` | body overlap: arms lag, head nods, torso squashes (0 = off, 2 = rubbery) |
| `grip` | no | [0.1, 0] | where a held prop sits, in the hand frame |
| `handZ` | no | 1 | 1 = hand over the forearm, -1 = under it |

## 4. `build`: a body from numbers

`build.heads` sets the height and, with it, defaults for everything else; any other number
overrides one default. Only `heads` and `muscle` are clamped; other numbers outside the range still draw but look wrong. Depths are side-view thicknesses (front to back), radii are limb radii,
all in head heights. With u = (heads - 2.2) / 5.8, clamped to 0..1, each default is
`toddler + (adult - toddler) * u`:

| Field | Default at 2.2 heads | at 8 heads | Sensible range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `heads` | | | 2.2 .. 8 (the engine clamps to 2 .. 9) | total height in head heights, 2.2 (toddler) to 8 (tall adult); default 3 |
| `legs` | 0.32 | 0.47 | 0.28 .. 0.52 | share of the height that is leg (sole to hip) |
| `arms` | 0.28 | 0.385 | 0.25 .. 0.45 | share of the height that is arm (shoulder to fingertip) |
| `neck` | 0.075 | 0.11 | 0.05 .. 0.2 | neck radius |
| `neckLength` | 0.06 | 0.3 | 0 .. 1.2 | neck length (base to jaw); a longer neck shortens the torso so the height stays `heads` |
| `shoulders` | 0.5 | 0.92 | 0.4 .. 1.3 | torso depth at the shoulders |
| `chest` | 0.52 | 0.95 | 0.4 .. 1.3 | torso depth at the chest |
| `waist` | 0.5 | 0.78 | 0.35 .. 1.3 | torso depth at the waist |
| `hips` | 0.52 | 0.86 | 0.4 .. 1.3 | torso depth at the hips |
| `belly` | 0.07 | 0 | 0 .. 0.7 | extra forward bulge of the belly (0.5 = very fat) |
| `seat` | 0.03 | 0.06 | 0 .. 0.2 | backward bulge of the bottom |
| `bust` | 0 | 0 | 0 .. 0.15 | forward bulge of the chest (0.05-0.1) |
| `arm` | 0.08 | 0.2 | 0.05 .. 0.3 | upper-arm radius (elbow 0.76x, wrist 0.58x) |
| `leg` | 0.135 | 0.31 | 0.1 .. 0.45 | thigh radius (knee 0.68x, ankle 0.49x) |
| `muscle` | 0 | 0 | 0 .. 1 (clamped) | 0..1: thicker arms (+45%) and legs (+30%), deeper chest and shoulders |
| `hand` | 1 | 1 | 0.6 .. 1.5 | hand size factor (hand length is 0.2 head at 2.2 heads, 0.62 at 8) |
| `foot` | 1 | 1 | 0.6 .. 1.5 | foot size factor (foot length 0.42 head at 2.2, 1.08 at 8) |
| `headWidth` | 0.96 | 0.8 | 0.7 .. 1.1 | front-to-back size of the generated head |
| `hide` | [] | | list | generated groups to leave out: any of `head` (the whole generated head with its face and hair cap), `hair` (only the hair cap: bald), `neck`, `torso`, `pelvis`, `arm`, `leg`, `foot` |

Typical bodies: toddler `{ heads: 2.3 }`; child `{ heads: 3.5 }`; teen `{ heads: 6.2 }`; adult
`{ heads: 7.5 }`; fat `{ belly: 0.55, chest: 1.05, waist: 1.0, hips: 0.98, arm: 0.17, leg: 0.3 }`;
thin `{ chest: 0.72, waist: 0.52, hips: 0.78, arm: 0.1, leg: 0.16 }`; muscular `{ muscle: 1, shoulders: 1.05 }`.

`proportions` (optional, overrides what `build` derives; required numbers if a skin has no
`build`): `head` 1, `neck`, `torso`, `shoulderDrop` (shoulder below the torso top),
`upperArm`, `foreArm`, `thigh`, `shin`, `ankleHeight`, `heel` and `toe` (pivots in the foot
frame), `footGround` (contact points in the foot frame), `farShoulder` ([x, y] offset of the
far shoulder), `radius` (`hip`, `knee`, `shoulder`, `elbow`, `wrist`, `neck`, `hem`).

**What the generated body draws** (palette names in brackets): arm and leg tubes [skin,
skinShade], a torso and pelvis in a plain body suit with short legs [suit, suitShade], a neck
[skin], shoes [shoe, sole], a plain head with ear, cheek, a hair cap [hair] and face swaps, and
hand swaps sized to the body. Everything the skin's own `parts` give for a group is drawn **on
top of** the generated group, so garments go straight on. A skin that gives `parts.head`
replaces the generated head; `swaps.eye` (etc.) replace that generated swap.

## 5. `parts`

`parts` maps a part key (2) to one entry or a list of entries, drawn in order. Entry kinds:

| Entry | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `{ d, fill, opacity }` | a filled SVG path in the part's frame (`M L C Q A Z`, absolute or relative) |
| `{ d, stroke, w }` | a stroked path, width `w` head units, round caps |
| `{ swap: 'eye' }` | draw the current eye / mouth / brow swap here (head only; added at the end if missing) |
| `{ tube: [r0, r1, r2], from, to, flat, inset, fill }` | (`arm`, `leg`) a soft limb: one continuous shape through the joint, radii at the three joints. `from`/`to` = fractions of the limb length (0 = shoulder or hip, 1 = wrist or ankle, up to 1.1). `flat`: 'start', 'end' or 'both' cuts an end straight. `inset: -0.35` = a strip along the back edge (+ = front) |
| `{ cap: [r0, r1], from, to, inset, fill }` or `{ cap: [r0, rMid, r1], mid, ... }` | (`upperArm` .. `shin`) a tapered capsule on one bone; with 3 radii `mid` (default 0.45) is where the middle radius sits along the bone |
| `{ ..., upright: true }` | (`holdNear`, `holdFar` only) draw this entry in an upright frame at the grip point instead of the hand frame, so it hangs straight down whatever the hand does (a lantern, a bag) |
| `{ ..., use: 'cane', length }` | (`holdNear` only) a walking stick: planted in step with the walk, carried in other actions (see the recipe) |

**Hands and held objects.** `parts.hand` replaces the hand swaps for **both** hands with one
fixed drawing (a mitten or a hook); usually leave it out and let the swaps change. `parts.holdNear`
and `parts.holdFar` draw an object in that hand through every action (hand frame, or
`upright: true`); the hand closes to `grip` while it holds, unless an action shapes the hand.
The grip point is `grip` (default [0.1, 0] in the hand frame).

**Garments** (they need `build`; they follow the body's own shape, so they fit any numbers):

| Garment | Entry | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sleeve, cuff, glove | `arm: { cover: [from, to] or true, loose, fill, flat, inset }` (0 = shoulder, 1 = wrist) | short sleeve `[0, 0.3]`, long sleeve `[0, 0.95]` |
| shorts, trousers, socks, boots | `leg: { cover: [from, to] or true, loose, fill, flat, inset }` (0 = hip, 1 = ankle) | shorts `[0, 0.35]`, trousers `[0, 1]`, boots `[0.78, 1.02]` |
| top, bodice, coat body | `torso: { cover: [from, to], loose, fill }` or `cover: true` | from/to = fractions of the torso height (0 = hip line, 1 = shoulders; `true` = the whole torso, -0.06 .. 1.1) |
| skirt, dress, kilt, robe | `skirt: { skirt: true, length, top, flare, loose, fill, shade, hem: { fill, w } }` | see below |

`loose` is extra thickness in head units (default 0). A cover drawn twice with `inset` gives
its shade strip. Covers are drawn in the order written, so a later cover lies on an earlier one
(a cardigan over a shirt). A torso cover stops at the hip line; anything that hangs lower (a
coat tail, a long apron, a tunic) is a `skirt`, because only the skirt bends at the hip and
follows the thighs when the body sits.

**Skirt.** Cloth from the waist round **both** legs down to `length` (0 = at the hips,
0.5 = knee, 1 = ankle, fraction of the leg), drawn over the legs. It is traced every frame from
the legs' real positions: it hangs and curves in slowly below the widest point, lies over the
thighs and shins when the body sits, widens with the stride but only as far as the cloth allows
(in a long run the lower legs come out from under the hem), and its hem trails on a spring (wind
moves it too). A skirt also makes coat tails, a long apron (`top: 0`) or a tunic skirt. `top` = waist height as a fraction of the torso (default 0.38); `flare` = how far the
hem spreads past the legs, as a fraction of the skirt length (default 0.15; 0.25-0.35 for a
long full dress); `loose` = ease round the legs (default 0.04); `shade` = a **colour name** for the far
leg's half (optional; note a chain's `shade` is a number); `hem` = a band along the hem (optional). Draw the bodice with
`torso: { cover: [0.3, 1.1], fill }` in the same colour. Below the hem the legs and shoes show.

**Draw order (`layer`)**, back to front: `back`, `arm.far`, `leg.far`, `pelvis`, `leg.near`,
`neck`, `torso` (skirt, then torso parts), `head` (head, then `hair`), `arm.near`, `front`.
Inside a layer the ink outline of every shape is drawn first and all fills after, so shapes of
one layer merge without seams. Parts of one key are drawn in the order written; chains come
after the parts of their layer. `back` is behind the whole body: something on that layer shows
only where it sticks out past the body's outline.

## 6. `motion`

| Field | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `weight` | 0.3 | 0 light .. 1 heavy: slower starts and stops, lower jumps, less bounce, more squash and jiggle of the torso |
| `energy` | 0.5 | 0 tired .. 1 lively: cadence, bounce, arm swing, jump height, quicker actions |
| `age` | 'adult' | 'baby' toddles (short quick steps, arms held out, leaning back), 'child', 'adult', 'elder' (shorter slower steps, no flight in a run, low jumps, a stoop) |
| `posture` | 0 (0.5 for elder) | -1 proud .. 1 stooped: rounded back, neck forward, head up |

Always on, from the body's own numbers: stride in leg lengths and cadence slower for longer
legs; jump height in leg lengths; hands are kept out of the head and out of the chest and belly
(they rest over the front of a big belly, or are held out when the arms are short); feet stand on
the ground. Every action in `docs/AUTHORING.md` works from 2.2 to 8 heads and thin to obese.

## 7. `palette`

Colour names used by parts. Any `<name>Shade` that is not in the palette is made
automatically by darkening `<name>` by `palette.shade` (default 0.82), so `jeansShade` works as
soon as `jeans` exists. A fill may also be a literal `#rrggbb`; an unknown name draws magenta.

The generated body uses: `skin`, `skinShade` (limbs, neck, face), `suit`, `suitShade` (the
plain body suit on torso, pelvis and the top of the legs: it is **grey** (#8a94a6) unless you
set it, and shows at the neck, shoulders and hips wherever your garments leave gaps, so set
`suit` to the colour of the main garment or the skin; `suitShade` and `skinShade` follow
`suit` and `skin` automatically unless you set them), `shoe`, `sole`, `hair` (the generated
hair cap and the brows), `eye`, `white` (eye highlights, teeth), `mouth`, `cheek`, and
`outline` (the ink line).

## 8. `swaps`

Named drawings the engine picks per frame. Kinds and the names actions ask for (a missing name
falls back to the first one):

| Kind | Frame | Names |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hand` | hand frame | `relaxed`, `fist`, `open`, `point`, `grip`, `thumb` (thumb up) |
| `eye` | head frame | `open`, `wide`, `narrow`, `closed`, `happy`, `sad` (an entry with `look: 1` follows the gaze) |
| `brow` | head frame | `neutral`, `up`, `down`, `worried` |
| `mouth` | head frame | `neutral`, `smile`, `open`, `o`, `worried`, `grit`, `sad` |

Syntax: each kind maps names to one entry or a list of entries (any part entry kind); brows
are strokes in the head frame just above the eye (the generated ones sit at y = 0.67-0.72):

```js
swaps: {
  eye: {
    open:   [{ d: 'M0.24 0.55A0.05 0.07 0 1 0 0.34 0.55A0.05 0.07 0 1 0 0.24 0.55Z', fill: 'eye', look: 1 },
             { d: 'M0.3 0.58A0.015 0.015 0 1 0 0.33 0.58A0.015 0.015 0 1 0 0.3 0.58Z', fill: 'white', look: 1 }],
    closed: { d: 'M0.24 0.56Q0.29 0.52 0.34 0.56', stroke: 'eye', w: 0.022 },
    happy:  { d: 'M0.24 0.54Q0.29 0.6 0.34 0.54', stroke: 'eye', w: 0.026 },
  },
  brow: { neutral: { d: 'M0.22 0.67Q0.28 0.7 0.36 0.68', stroke: 'brow', w: 0.035 },
          up:      { d: 'M0.22 0.71Q0.28 0.75 0.36 0.72', stroke: 'brow', w: 0.035 },
          down:    { d: 'M0.21 0.7Q0.28 0.69 0.37 0.63', stroke: 'brow', w: 0.04 },
          worried: { d: 'M0.22 0.65Q0.28 0.67 0.35 0.72', stroke: 'brow', w: 0.034 } },
  mouth: { neutral: { d: 'M0.33 0.24Q0.37 0.235 0.41 0.25', stroke: 'mouth', w: 0.02 },
           smile:   { d: 'M0.32 0.27Q0.36 0.2 0.42 0.25', stroke: 'mouth', w: 0.022 } },
}
```

A skin's swaps replace the generated ones kind by kind (giving `eye` keeps the generated
mouth and brows). Where they draw: the `{ swap: 'eye' }` entries in `parts.head`, or on top
of the head if `parts.head` has none.

## 8b. Face swaps (expressions and speech)

All face swaps are drawn in the head frame (origin top of the neck, x forward, y up, 1 = head
height). On the generated head the mouth is at (0.38 W, 0.24), the eye at (0.3 W, 0.55), the brow
at y 0.67-0.72 (W = `build.headWidth`, about 0.8-0.95). On a **drawn profile head** measure from
F, the x of the face's front edge at that height (the cheek line, not the nose tip): mouth centre at
(F - 0.15, 0.18-0.22), eye centre at (F - 0.2, 0.55-0.6), brow centred over the eye at y 0.68-0.72
and 0.14 wide. A head whose face edge is at 0.4 therefore wants the mouth near (0.25, 0.21), not
(0.38, 0.24), which would float in front of the lips. Check with `node tools/say.cjs out.png
--skin=films/<film>/skins/<name>.js --shapes`.

| Kind | Names the engine asks for | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mouth` | `rest`, `mbp`, `ah`, `ee`, `oh`, `oo`, `fv`, `l`, `wq` | speaking (`docs/SPEECH.md`) |
| `mouth` | `neutral`, `smile`, `open`, `o`, `worried`, `grit`, `sad` | faces and moods, and action keys (`mouth: 'o'`) |
| `eye` | `open`, `closed`, `wide`, `narrow`, `happy`, `sad` | blinks use `closed`; moods use the others |
| `brow` | `neutral`, `up`, `down`, `worried` | moods; lifted a little on spoken emphasis |

**Fallbacks.** A missing name never breaks a face. Eyes and brows fall back to `open` and
`neutral`; mood mouths to `neutral` or `smile`; a missing speech mouth to the nearest shape the
skin has, scaled about its centre (`ah` -> `open`, `ee` -> `grit` or a squashed `open`,
`oh` -> `o` or a narrowed `open`, `oo`/`wq` -> each other, `o` or a small `open`, `fv` ->
`grit` or closed, `l` -> a squashed `open`, `rest`/`mbp` -> `neutral` or `closed`). The
smallest set that talks: `open` and `closed` (or `neutral`). Recommended: the seven mood mouths;
best: all nine speech mouths as well. The swap name `closed` is a synonym the fallbacks know for
a shut mouth.

**The generated face** (a skin with `build` that gives no `swaps.mouth`, `swaps.brow` or eye
swaps of its own) is drawn from numbers instead: a mouth from open, width and roundness with
teeth and tongue, a smile-to-frown blend, brows with height and angle, and upper lids that
close by degrees. A skin that gives `swaps.mouth` keeps the generated brows and eyes, and the
other way round (each kind is replaced on its own).

**Beards.** A `parts.head` or `parts.hair` piece moves with the jaw while speaking exactly when
the box of its path's points (control points included) has bottom below y 0.12, top below 0.62,
height at least 0.12 and vertical centre below 0.32. A beard reaching the chin passes. A
moustache (bottom above 0.12) does not: it stays on the upper lip, as a real one does, and so does
anything reaching above 0.62 (hair joined to a beard). Draw a beard as its own path, separate from
the hair and the moustache, so it is found.

Swap syntax is as in section 8: `mouth: { ah: { d, fill }, mbp: { d, stroke, w }, ... }`, one
entry or a list per name. Keep each mouth in the same place so that changes do not jump.

## 9. `chains` (springs)

Hair locks, scarf tails, backpacks, hems: simulated from t = 0 with gravity, drag, wind and the
body's real motion. Fields: `bone` (head, neck, torso, pelvis), `at` (anchor in that frame),
`rest` (degrees: 0 forward, 90 up, 180 back, 270 down), `curl`, `seg` (lengths), `width` (one
more than `seg`), `fill`, `shade`, `shadeSide`, `layer`, `tip`, `stiff` (0 loose .. 1 rigid),
`limit` (max swing in degrees, default 120), `gravity` (1), `drag`, `wind` (1), `inertia`
(0.6), `freq`, `end` + `endUpright` (a part at the tip, e.g. a backpack). `shade` here is a
number 0..1 (the width of a darker strip). Details: `docs/AUTHORING.md`, "Spring chains".

**Layer for small hanging things.** The default `layer` is `back`, which is drawn behind the
whole body, so a short chain that hangs inside the body's outline (an earring, a strand over
the shoulder) is hidden. Use `layer: 'head'` for things on the head or face (earrings, a
fringe), `layer: 'torso'` for things lying on the back or chest (a braid down the back, a
necklace pendant, straps), and `back` only for things that hang out behind the body (a
ponytail, a cape, a backpack).

## 10. Minimal skins

A person from numbers only (this is already correct and well shaped):

```js
(function (g) {
  (g.CharSkins = g.CharSkins || {}).nora = { name: 'nora', extends: 'mannequin',
    build: { heads: 7, chest: 0.8, waist: 0.6, hips: 0.85 },
    motion: { energy: 0.7 },
    palette: { suit: '#3f6fa8', hair: '#5a3a28' } };
})(typeof self !== 'undefined' ? self : this);
```

The same person dressed: a T-shirt, jeans, boots, a ponytail and a skirt-free look:

```js
(function (g) {
  (g.CharSkins = g.CharSkins || {}).nora = { name: 'nora', extends: 'mannequin',
    build: { heads: 7, chest: 0.8, waist: 0.6, hips: 0.85 },
    motion: { energy: 0.7 },
    palette: { shirt: '#e2574c', jeans: '#3d5a8a', boot: '#5a3a28', hair: '#5a3a28' },
    parts: {
      torso: { cover: true, loose: 0.02, fill: 'shirt' },
      arm: { cover: [0, 0.3], loose: 0.02, flat: 'end', fill: 'shirt' },
      leg: [{ cover: [0, 1], loose: 0.02, fill: 'jeans' }, { cover: [0, 1], loose: 0.02, inset: -0.35, fill: 'jeansShade' },
        { cover: [0.8, 1.02], loose: 0.03, flat: 'start', fill: 'boot' }],
      hair: { d: 'M-0.5 0.6C-0.55 1.0 0.1 1.15 0.42 0.82C0.2 0.9 -0.1 0.85 -0.3 0.7Z', fill: 'hair' },
    },
    chains: { tail: { bone: 'head', at: [-0.45, 0.85], rest: 200, seg: [0.25, 0.22], width: [0.16, 0.14, 0.04],
      fill: 'hair', layer: 'back', stiff: 0.35 } } };
})(typeof self !== 'undefined' ? self : this);
```

## 11. Recipes

All in one skin that `extends: 'mannequin'`; coordinates for a 6-7 head body (scale by the
tables in 2).

- **Hat**: `hair: { d: 'M-0.55 0.92C-0.5 1.3 0.45 1.3 0.5 0.92Z', fill: 'hat' }` plus a brim
  `{ d: 'M-0.62 0.9L0.62 0.9L0.6 0.97L-0.6 0.97Z', fill: 'hatShade' }`. Add `build.hide: ['hair']`
  so the generated hair cap does not show under the brim, and draw any hair you want below the hat.
- **Moustache and brows**: in `parts.hair` (it is drawn over the face):
  `{ d: 'M0.24 0.26C0.34 0.32 0.48 0.3 0.54 0.22C0.44 0.2 0.32 0.18 0.24 0.26Z', fill: 'stache' }`;
  thick brows: `swaps.brow` with strokes of `w: 0.06` at y 0.68.
- **Glasses**: `parts.hair` entries `{ d: 'M0.24 0.55A0.08 0.08 0 1 0 0.4 0.55A0.08 0.08 0 1 0 0.24 0.55Z', stroke: 'frame', w: 0.02 }`
  and an arm `{ d: 'M0.24 0.55L-0.04 0.52', stroke: 'frame', w: 0.018 }`.
- **Apron**: a bib `torso: { cover: [0.35, 0.8], loose: 0.05, fill: 'apron' }` (after the shirt)
  and a `skirt: { skirt: true, top: 0, length: 0.55, fill: 'apron' }`.
- **Open cardigan or coat over a shirt**: `torso: [{ cover: true, fill: 'shirt' },
  { cover: true, loose: 0.04, fill: 'coat' }, { d: <a strip down the front, x from 0.15 to front>, fill: 'shirt' }]`;
  long coat tails: `skirt: { skirt: true, top: 0.25, length: 0.45, flare: 0.1, fill: 'coat' }`.
- **Hood and pocket**: hood down = a chain-free shape in `hairBack` behind the head
  (`{ d: 'M-0.2 0.1C-0.7 0.1 -0.75 0.7 -0.4 0.8L-0.1 0.4Z', fill: 'hoodie' }`); pocket = a torso path
  over the cover around y = 0.2-0.35 of the torso height, x near the front.
- **Backpack**: a strap path on the torso cover, and a chain
  `{ bone: 'torso', at: [-0.4, 0.8 * torsoHeight], rest: 265, seg: [0.1], width: [0.04, 0.04],
  fill: 'strap', layer: 'back', stiff: 0.3, limit: 40, endUpright: true, end: { d: <pack drawn
  hanging below 0, at negative x>, fill: 'pack' } }`.
- **Earrings**: a chain `{ bone: 'head', at: [-0.06, 0.4], rest: 270, seg: [0.06, 0.05],
  width: [0.02, 0.02, 0.02], fill: 'gold', layer: 'head', stiff: 0.2, end: { d: 'M0 -0.04A0.04 0.04 0 1 0 0 0.04A0.04 0.04 0 1 0 0 -0.04Z', fill: 'gold' } }`.
- **Held object**: a walking stick
  `holdNear: { use: 'cane', length: 2.6, d: 'M-0.025 0.05L0.025 0.05L0.025 -2.6L-0.025 -2.6Z', fill: 'wood' }`
  (drawn hanging down from the grip, `length` = its length, about 0.45 x heads). With
  `use: 'cane'` the engine plants its tip beside the near foot and steps it with the walk while
  standing or walking (the hand holds its top), and carries it held out forward in runs,
  jumps, gestures and sitting, never into the ground. A bag or lantern that hangs straight:
  `holdFar: { upright: true, d: <drawn hanging below 0>, fill }`; a mug in the hand frame:
  `holdNear: { d: 'M0.08 -0.06L0.22 -0.06L0.22 0.1L0.08 0.1Z', fill: 'mug' }`.

## 12. Errors

A skin with a JavaScript syntax error does not load: `node tools/check.cjs films/<film>` prints
`ERROR line 0: films/<film>/skins/<name>.js fails to load: <the JavaScript message>` and, because
the skin is then missing, an error on the `actor ... = skin <name>` line. An unknown colour name
draws magenta; an unknown part key or field is ignored (`tools/skincheck.cjs` reports it).

## 13. Glossary (common names)

part key = the **parent** bone; frame origin = the **pivot**; the frame's angle = the bone's
**rotation**, set by the engine; `layer` = draw order; `parts` = the drawings.


========================================
FILE: docs/AUTHORING.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/AUTHORING.md
========================================

# Authoring a CharAI film

A film is a folder with one script, `film.char`. CharAI draws the set, the actors, the
camera and the text from it. You write what happens and when; you never draw frames.

**A script is one `.char` file or a film folder.** A single file is the quickest way to start:
`node tools/check.cjs examples/hello.char` (also `render.cjs`, `sheet.cjs`, `export.cjs`). Its own
folder plays the film folder: `skins/`, `actions/`, `props/`, `lines/` next to it win over the shared ones,
and the page is written next to it as `<name>.html`. A folder with `film.char` works as before
(page `index.html`). Seven runnable examples, one idea each, are in `examples/` (see `examples/README.md`).

```
films/<name>/film.char        the script (required)
films/<name>/skins|sets|puppets|props/*.js   your own library files (optional; they win over shared ones)
```

## Layout, bare stage and Char.mount

Run everything from the engine folder. Paths: engine files in `src/`, example skins in `skins/`
(`tess.js kai.js mannequin.js`, worked examples, not a character library), optional scenery and
creatures in `extras/sets|puppets|props/`, regression films in `films/`, a host page in
`examples/host.html`. A film's own `skins|sets|puppets|props/` still win over the shared ones.
Tests: `node --test tests/*.cjs`. `tools/shot.cjs` needs `puppeteer-core` (installed in this
folder, or set `CHAR_PUPPETEER`, or `"puppeteer"` in the untracked `.char-local.json`; run `npm install` otherwise).

**Bare stage (characters only).** A film needs no `set` line. Without one the background is
transparent, the ground is flat and there is no scenery. Optional header line, all parts optional:

```
stage width=2400 ground=600 scale=68    # world width px, ground y px, px per head height (these are the defaults)
```

Anchors `left`, `center`, `right` (x 200, 640, 1080) exist; plain numbers work too. With a
`set` line nothing changes. See `films/bare-test/film.char`.

**Char.mount (for a host page).** Load `src/rig.js gait.js poses.js clips.js perform.js`, your
skin files, then `src/script.js stage.js`. Then:

```js
const m = Char.mount(document.getElementById('chars'), { script: text, skins: CharSkins, width: 1280, height: 720 });
m.duration; m.seek(t); m.destroy();   // seek(t) is a pure function of t, any order
```

It draws only the characters on a transparent SVG layer, so the host paints its own scenery
behind it (keep the host's ground line at the script's `ground=`). See `examples/host.html`.

## Commands (run from the engine folder)

```
node tools/check.cjs films/<name> [--timeline]   # errors + motion problems; writes index.html; exit 1 on errors
node tools/sheet.cjs films/<name> sheet.png --n=12   # one PNG of 12 evenly spaced frames with timestamps
node tools/sheet.cjs films/<name> jump.png --n=12 --from=5.6 --to=7.4   # a close strip of one action
node tools/render.cjs films/<name> out.mp4 --fps=24  # 1280x720 MP4 (about 1.4 s per second of film)
```

Work in this loop: write the script, `check` until it says `OK`, look at one `sheet`, fix, then
`render`. `--timeline` prints when every line starts and ends, useful for `+` times. Every
message names the line to change and what to write. Open `index.html` in a browser to play.

## Example (`films/demo`)

```
film "Lantern Light" 10s
set hillside dusk
actor Tess = skin tess at 230
actor Ren = skin ren at 1160 facing left
puppet Pip = bird at branch facing left
prop lantern at 532

0.0  Tess: walk(to=490), face(happy)
+0.1 Tess: hold(lantern)              # 0.1 s after Tess's walk ends
0.4  caption: "Dusk on the hill.", for=2.4
2.0  Ren: look(at=down), face(sad)
3.0  cam: pan(to=1040, over=3), zoom(1.2, over=3)
+0.2 Tess: walk(to=860, speed=1.4)
3.4  Pip: fly(to=1290)
+0.3 Pip: hop(to=1236)
4.8  Ren: look(at=Tess), face(surprised)
+0.3 Ren: wave()
5.6  caption: "There you are!", by=Ren, for=2
+0.1 Tess: face(happy)
7.6  Ren: face(happy)
8.6  card: "Light finds friends."
```

A second example with the new motion (a hero close-up in a gust, then running, a hop, a skid):

```
film "Gust" 14s
set hillside
actor Kai = skin kai at 380
0    cam: cut(to=Kai, zoom=2), frame(on=Kai, top=head, bottom=thigh, x=0.35, over=0)
0    Kai: idle()
0.4  wind: gust(amount=1, over=1.8)
1.6  Kai: face(happy)
2.6  cam: home(over=1.2)
2.6  cam: follow(Kai, over=0.8)
3.0  Kai: bounce(times=3)
+0   Kai: run(to=700)
+0   Kai: jump(to=900, height=1.2)
+0   Kai: run(to=1200, end=skid)
+0.15 Kai: turn()
+0.05 Kai: wave(hand=both), face(excited)
```

## Grammar

One statement per line. `#` starts a comment. Names are case-sensitive.

Header lines (before or between timed lines):

| Line | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `film "Title" 30s` | title and length in seconds (required, first) |
| `set <name> [variant]` | one set per film, e.g. `set hillside dusk` |
| `actor <Name> = skin <skin> at <place> [facing left] [scale=1]` | a person drawn by a skin |
| `puppet <Name> = <kind> at <place> [facing left] [scale=1]` | an animal or creature |
| `prop <kind> [as <Name>] [at <place>]` | an object; without `at` it appears when first held |

Timed lines: `<time> <target>: call(args)[, call(args)]`

- `<time>`: absolute seconds (`3`, `4.5`) or `+n`: n seconds after the **same target's**
  previous line has finished (a walk finishes when the actor arrives and settles). `+0` = right after.
- Calls on one line start together and must use different channels (see tables).
- Arguments: positional in the listed order, or `key=value`. Values: numbers, names, `"text"`.
  `face(scared)` = `face(mood=scared)`.
- A target's lines must go forward in time. A new line on the same channel before a move
  finishes is an error (the move would be cut): use `+0` or a later time.

**Places** (`at`, `to`, `pan`): an x in set pixels (0 = left edge of the set), an anchor
of the set, or the name of an actor, puppet or prop (where it was placed at the start).
`y` comes from the ground, or from the anchor.

## Actors

Channels: **body** (one at a time, holds until the next body action), **arms** (gesture over
the body), **face**, **look**. Required arguments have no `=`.

| Channel | Call | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| body | `walk(to, speed=1)` | speed 0.5..2 |
| body | `run(to, speed=1, end=stop)` | a pumping run (speed 0.5..2.5, see Speeds below); starts with an anticipation beat; `end=skid` arrives at full speed and skids to a stop at `to` |
| body | `sneak(to, speed=1)` | tiptoe, crouched |
| body | `enter(from=left, speed=1)` | walk in from off screen to the `at` place |
| body | `jump(to, height=1)` | crouch, stretch, tuck, squash on landing, recover; height 2 = big; `to` = where she lands (to hop over something, aim about 1.5 leg lengths past it) |
| body | `skid()` | stop from a run on the spot: brace, slide, overshoot, settle (`run(..., end=skid)` is usually better) |
| body | `bounce(times=3)` | bounce on the toes, `times` bobs |
| body | `turn()` | face the other way: a quick dip and hop-pivot on the back foot, the feet re-planted under her (0.48 s) |
| body | `stand()`, `idle()` | idle = standing with life (weight shifts, a glance, breathing); holds until the next body line |
| body | `kneel()`, `crouch()`, `recoil()` | recoil = flinch and step back in fear |
| body | `sit(on=0)` | on = seat height in px |
| arms | `wave(hand=near)` | near, far or both (both = flung up, out of step, a laughing bob) |
| arms | `point(at, for=1.5)`, `reach(at, for=1.2)` | at = a place or name |
| arms | `cheer()` | both arms up |
| arms | `hold(prop, how=front)` | how = up, front, side; keeps holding |
| arms | `drop()` | the prop falls to the ground (`quiet=1`: no gesture) |
| pair | `hug(with=B, speed=1)` | a paired action: A walks up, both play their role (docs/PAIRS.md): hug, handshake, highfive, pat, shove, punchblock, punchfall, give(prop=), throwto(prop=). `speed=` or `for=` (seconds) set the length; the line occupies both actors, so either one's next `+0` waits for it; afterwards they stand apart |
| props | `pickup(prop=box)`, `sit(on=chair)`, `knock(on=door)` | walks to the prop first; grip, weight, seat, upright: docs/PROPS.md |
| face | `face(mood=neutral)` | happy, scared, determined, surprised, sad, neutral, excited, angry, tired, proud, shy |
| mood | `mood(name=neutral, strength=1)` | colours every motion until the next mood line: neutral, happy, sad, angry, scared, tired, proud, shy (`docs/ACTIONS.md`) |
| body / arms | action files | `bow`, `shrug`, `clap`, `pickup`, `stomp`, `slump`, `lookaround`, `stumble` and any file in `actions/` or the film's `actions/`: see `docs/ACTIONS.md` |
| look | `look(at=front)` | a place or name, or up, down, front, back. At a name the head aims at that actor's eyes and follows them; the pitch stays within about 25 degrees down and 30 up. It holds until the next `look`: `look(at=front)` releases it |
| look | `nod()` | |

Moving actors face the way they go. Walking speed depends on the skin's legs (about
80-130 px/s for walk); `check --timeline` shows the real end times.

**Chaining body lines.** A body line whose time falls before the previous body move has finished
is an error in `check` ("... runs until 6.02s, but this line starts ... and cuts it short"). To
chain moves write `+0` (starts the moment the previous one ends) or `+0.2` (a small pause);
use `check --timeline` to see when each move really ends.

**Speeds and timing** (a child skin of about 2.7 heads at actorScale 68; scale with actorScale):

| Move | speed=1 | speed=2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| walk | 100 px/s | 200 px/s |
| run (top speed) | about 285 px/s | about 515 px/s (longer stride, a flight phase, more lean) |
| run 500 px, `end=stop` | 2.7 s | 2.0 s |
| run 500 px, `end=skid` (the last ~90-170 px are the skid) | 3.1 s | 2.2 s |

A run spends about 0.4 s getting up to speed (an anticipation beat, then the ramp) and 0.5 s
stopping (`end=stop`) or 1.35 s skidding and settling (`end=skid`). A jump takes about
1.1 s + 0.05 s per leg length of distance on the ground, times sqrt(height): 150 px = 1.6 s,
300 px = 1.75 s, 450 px = 1.9 s at height 1 (a leg length is about 65 px here). `turn` takes
0.48 s, `bounce(times=n)` 0.9 s + 0.4 s per bob, `wave` 1.75 s (both hands 1.9 s).

How it moves (nothing to write, but good to know): `idle`, `bounce`, `jump`, `skid`, `turn`,
the start of `run` and `wave` are played from motion clips (`clips.js`: pose keys on a time line,
splines, the head and arms trailing the hips, feet planted by contact marks). Each action
cross-fades from whatever came before, including from a running gait. On top of that the
engine simulates springs from t = 0: hair tufts, scarf, backpack and hem swing with the body's
real motion, gravity and wind; arms and head lag a little and settle; the torso squashes on
landings. Every frame is still the same whatever order you seek in. Write `+0` between body
lines: a body line that starts before the previous one has finished cuts it short.

## Wind: `wind`

| Call | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `gust(amount=1, over=1.5, from=right)` | a gust: rises in the first quarter of `over`, dies away by the end. amount 1 = strong (lifts hair and scarf well clear), 0.4 = a breath. `from=right` blows toward the left. |
| `blow(amount=0.3, over=1, from=right)` | a steady wind from now on, reached over `over` s; `blow(amount=0)` calms it |

Gusts add to the steady wind. Only spring chains feel the wind (sets draw their own weather).

## Puppets

A puppet does one state per line: `Pip: fly(to=branch)`. States that move need `to=`; the
others take `for=<seconds>`. `turn` flips it. States switch smoothly.

`bird` (44 px tall): `perch` (default, holds), `hop(to)` (hops along the ground), `flap`
(1.2 s), `fly(to)` (arcs through the air, 260 px/s), `peck` (1.35 s), `sing` (1.5 s). After
a timed or moving state it returns to `perch`.

## Camera: `cam`

| Call | Channel | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pan(to, over=1.5)` | pos | centre the camera on a place or name |
| `follow(target, over=0.8)` | pos | keep an actor or puppet centred until the next pan or cut |
| `cut(to, zoom=0)` | pos | jump instantly (zoom=0 keeps the zoom) |
| `zoom(to, over=1)` | zoom | 1 = whole frame (minimum), 1.5 = closer |
| `shake(amount=8, over=0.6)` | shake | px, dying away |
| `fade(dir=out, over=0.6)` | fade | `out` to black, `in` back |
| `frame(on, top=head, bottom=thigh, x=0.35, over=1.2)` | frame | close-up on an actor (or two: `on=Kai+Tess` keeps both whole, heads, feet and hands, for any sizes; `pad=` widens it): the frame height runs from `top` to `bottom` and the actor stands at `x` of the frame width (0 = left edge, 0.5 = centre). It tracks the actor until `home()`. Levels: head, chin, chest, waist, hip, thigh, knee, feet. `over=0` = a cut. |
| `home(over=1.2)` | frame | leave the close-up: back to the pan / zoom / follow camera, which kept running underneath |

The camera starts centred at the set's start x. It stops at the set's edges, so it can never
show past them (check warns when a pan wants to go further). The camera's height follows the
ground: zoom 1-2 shows whole actors, zoom 3 is a waist-up close-up.

Hero close-up, then pull back to the whole body: `0 cam: frame(on=Baker, top=head, bottom=thigh,
x=0.33, over=0)`, then `3.5 cam: home(over=1.4)` with a `cam: cut(to=..., zoom=2)` or `follow`
underneath it from the start.

`frame` works out (k = px per head height of the actor = the set's `actorScale` times the
actor's `scale`; levels in head heights above the ground, `head` = the actor's full height):
`zoom = 720 / (k * (top - bottom) * 1.1 + 1)`, camera x = actor x - (x * 1280 - 640) / zoom,
camera y = ground y under the actor - k * (top + bottom) / 2 (then kept inside the set).
For a child skin of about 2.7 heads, head to thigh gives zoom about 4.5-4.8 at actorScale 68.

## Text: `caption` and `card`

- `caption: "text", for=3` shows a subtitle at the bottom (`at=top` for the top). A new
  caption replaces the old one; `caption: clear` removes it.
- `caption: "Hi!", by=Kai` draws a speech bubble above an actor or puppet.
- `card: "text"` fades a full-frame end card in and keeps it to the end; `for=2` makes it a
  title card that fades out; `sub="smaller line"` adds a second line.

Keep captions under about 60 characters.

## Shared library

- Sets: `hillside` (2400 x 720). Anchors: `left` 150, `path` 480, `center` 800, `hilltop`
  1250 (top of a gentle hill), `tree` 1640 (beside the trunk), `branch` (on the tree, above
  the ground), `rock` 2050, `right` 2260. Variants: `day` (default), `dawn`, `dusk`, `night`.
  The camera starts at x=640; at zoom 1 it shows 1280 px of the set.
- Skins: `tess` (a girl with a ponytail and scarf); the demo adds `ren`.
- Puppets: `bird`. Props: `lantern` (glows; shines best at dusk and night).

## Adding your own

Copy the example file into your film folder (or the shared folder), rename, edit. Each file
registers itself on a global; everything must be a pure function of time (no state between
frames). The top comment of each example lists every field.

- **Set** (`sets/hillside.js`): `width`, `height` 720, `ground(x)` (y in px, y grows down),
  `anchors` (`x` or `[x, y]`), `actorScale` (px per head height), `camera`, `palette` +
  `variants`, and `layers` `[{ depth, draw(ctx), static, front }]` back to front. Depth 0
  never moves, 1 is the actors' ground, above 1 with `front: true` passes in front of actors.
  Draw each layer from x = -100 to `1280 + (width - 1280) * depth + 100`.
  **Zoom and depth.** For camera centre (cx, cy) in set px and zoom z, a point (px, py) of a
  layer of depth d lands on screen at `((px - Cx) * s + 640, (py - Cy) * s + 360)` with
  `Cx = 640 + (cx - 640) * d`, `Cy = 360 + (cy - 360) * d`. The scale s is `1 + (z - 1) * d`
  (default), or with the set field **`dolly: true`** (the camera moves closer instead of
  magnifying): `s = 1 / (1 - d * (1 - 1/z))` for d < 1, and `1 + (z - 1) * d` for d >= 1. So
  depth 1 and the actors always scale by z; with dolly at z = 4.8 a depth-0.5 layer grows only
  1.65x (2.9x without), depth 0.1 1.09x, the sky (depth near 0) hardly at all. A set without the
  field renders exactly as before.
- **Puppet** (`puppets/bird.js`): `height`, `initial`, `states` (`loop`, `dur` + `then`,
  `travel: 'ground'|'air'` + `speed`, or `step`/`stepLength` for hopping), `pose(state,
  since, t)` returning numbers and `render(params)` returning SVG facing right with the feet
  at (0, 0). The stage blends the numbers between states, so return the same keys from
  every state.
- **Prop** (`props/lantern.js`): SVG with the grip at (0, 0), `base` (the point that rests on
  the ground), `hang` (swings from the hand) and optional `glow`.
- **Skin**: copy `skins/kai.js` (it uses every feature below) or `skins/tess.js` (plain, no
  outline) and read "Writing a skin" below. For a recolour, write only the difference:
  ```js
  (function (g) { (g.CharSkins = g.CharSkins || {}).ren = { name: 'ren', extends: 'tess',
    palette: { hair: '#231a16', top: '#d0573f' } }; })(globalThis);
  ```

## Writing a skin

**The full skin contract is `docs/RIG.md`** (every field, defaults, garments, the `build` body from
numbers and `motion`). The quickest correct person is a skin that `extends: 'mannequin'` and sets
`build` numbers and a palette (see `films/lineup/skins/`, `films/rig-example/` and `films/recipes/`). The notes below
cover the older hand-drawn skins (kai, tess) and spring-chain recipes.

A skin is one file of plain data (`skins/<name>.js`, registered on `CharSkins`). The rig is a
side view facing right; draw everything facing right. Units are head heights (head = 1), y up.

**Fields.** `name`; `proportions` (bone lengths: head 1, neck, torso, shoulderDrop, upperArm,
foreArm, thigh, shin, ankleHeight, heel/toe pivots and `footGround` contact points in the foot
frame, `radius`); `headTop` (top of the hair above the head origin, for height and framing);
`outline` (ink width in head units: 0 = flat, 0.022 thin, 0.035-0.045 thick and bold); `farShade`;
`palette` (`'<key>Shade'` = the darker tone of a key; `outline` = ink colour); `parts`; `swaps`
(hand: relaxed, fist, open, point, grip; eye: open, wide, narrow, closed, happy, sad; brow;
mouth: neutral, smile, open, o, worried, grit, sad); `chains`; `springs`; `grip`; `handZ`.

**Frames for parts.** torso and pelvis: origin = pelvis, x forward, y up (the torso runs up to
y = proportions.torso, the neck starts there). neck: origin = neck base. head: origin = top of
the neck. foot: origin = ankle, x along the sole. Hand swaps: origin = wrist, x along the
fingers. Per-bone limb parts (upperArm, foreArm, thigh, shin): x 0..1 along the bone. Entries:
`{ d, fill }`, `{ d, stroke, w }`, `{ cap: [r0, r1], from, to, inset, fill }`, `{ swap: 'eye' }`.

**Soft limbs (no hinge).** `parts.arm` and `parts.leg` draw a whole limb as one continuous tube
through the joint, with one unbroken outline and a soft crease inside the bend:
`{ tube: [rShoulder, rElbow, rWrist], fill }` (leg: hip, knee, ankle). `from`/`to` are fractions
of the whole limb length (0 = shoulder or hip, 1 = wrist or ankle; above 1 runs on past the
end), so a sleeve is `{ tube: [...], to: 0.3, flat: 'end', fill: 'top' }`, a boot
`{ tube: [...], from: 0.78, to: 1.01, flat: 'start', fill: 'shoe' }`. `flat`: 'start' | 'end' |
'both' cuts the end straight. `inset: -0.35` = the shade strip along the back edge (+ = front).
Per-bone parts still draw on top (seams, laces). Use these instead of per-bone `cap`s.

**Torso.** Draw the torso part in its frame as usual: the engine bends it along a short spine
and squashes or stretches it keeping its area (on landings, crouches, sudden stops), so draw it
as one or a few closed paths, not many small pieces near the top and bottom edges. Points above
y = torso follow the chest, points below 0 follow the hips. Torso-anchored chains move with it.

**Spring chains** (`chains: { name: {...} }`, drawn in the order written). Each chain is a row of
segments hanging from a bone, simulated with the body's real motion, gravity, air drag and wind,
and drawn as one tapered ribbon:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `bone` | head, neck, torso or pelvis |
| `at` | anchor in that bone's frame |
| `rest` | direction at rest in degrees in the bone frame (0 = forward, 90 = up, 180 = straight back, 270 = straight down) |
| `curl` | extra bend per segment, degrees (+ curls up/counter-clockwise) |
| `seg` | segment lengths, e.g. `[0.12, 0.1]` |
| `width` | ribbon width at each point (one more than `seg`), e.g. `[0.12, 0.08, 0.02]` |
| `fill`, `shade`, `shadeSide` | colour; shade strip width 0..1 along one side (1 = back side) |
| `layer` | draw layer: `back` (behind everything), `arm.far`, `leg.far`, `pelvis`, `leg.near`, `neck`, `torso`, `head` (over the face), `arm.near`, `front` |
| `tip` | how far the tip pokes past the last point |
| `stiff` | 0 = loose cloth, 0.3 = a scarf tail, 0.4-0.5 = springy hair tufts, 0.6-0.7 = a stiff hem; 1 = rigid (no simulation: a sword) |
| `limit` | most degrees it may swing from rest (default 120; 60-80 keeps a tuft off the face, 15-25 for a hem) |
| `gravity` | 1 = normal (default), 0 = weightless. The drawn rest shape is where it settles when standing still |
| `drag`, `wind`, `inertia` | air damping (default 4 + 2 stiff), how much it catches the wind (1), how hard it swings from the body's starts and stops (0.6; 1 = full) |
| `freq` | override the spring (Hz); default 0.8 + 4 * stiff |
| `end`, `endUpright` | a part drawn at the tip. Without `endUpright` its x axis runs along the last segment; with `endUpright: true` it is drawn in the bone's upright frame (x forward, y up), turned only as far as the chain swings: use this for a backpack or pouch |

Recipes (see `skins/kai.js`):
- *Several hair tufts*: one chain per tuft on `bone: 'head'`, each its own `at`, `rest`, `curl`,
  `seg` (2 segments) and tapering `width` ending near 0, `stiff` 0.35-0.5, `limit` 60-80. Tufts
  behind the head go on layer `back`, tufts over the crown or fringe on `head`. Mix `hair` and a
  second colour (e.g. orange tips) by giving tufts different fills. Keep the main hair mass a
  head part; the tufts are what moves.
- *Bunched scarf with a tail*: draw the bunched wrap in the torso part (a few overlapping
  rounded paths at y = torso .. torso + 0.15, with a shade path); add a tail chain on
  `bone: 'torso'` at the back of the wrap, `rest` 220-235, 3-4 segments, `stiff` 0.1-0.2,
  layer `back`; a short second chain for the knot ends if you like.
- *Backpack bouncing on its strap*: draw the strap across the chest in the torso part; add a
  chain on `bone: 'torso'` at the shoulder blade, `rest` about 265, one short segment (the strap
  drop, 0.08-0.12) with a thin `width`, `stiff` 0.3, `limit` 40, layer `back`, and the pack
  itself as `end` with `endUpright: true` (drawn hanging below the origin: y from 0 down to
  about -0.4).
- *Skirt or tunic hem that sways*: the dress top in the torso part ends at the hip line; the
  skirt is a wide, short chain: `bone: 'torso'`, `at: [0, -0.1]`, `rest: 268`, `seg` two of
  0.07-0.09, `width` the skirt width at each point (widening, e.g. [0.5, 0.56, 0.62]),
  `stiff` 0.6-0.7, `limit` 15-25, layer `torso`, a `shade` strip, and the darker hem band as
  `end` with `endUpright: true` (a stroke or thin path across y = 0).
- *Thick ink outline*: `outline: 0.04` and `palette.outline: '#3a2418'` (dark brown). Every
  part, tube and chain gets it; inner seams vanish because fills are drawn over all outlines of
  the same layer.

**Body springs.** `springs: { arms: 1, head: 1, torso: 1 }` sets how much the arms lag and
settle, the head nods on impacts and the torso squashes and bends against starts and stops
(0 = off, 1 = default, 2 = rubbery). Leave it out for the default 1.

**Check a new skin** with a little film (idle, jump, `run(..., end=skid)`, turn, wave and a
`wind: gust`): `check`, then `sheet --from --to` strips around the jump and the skid.

## Rules of thumb

- Give every actor something every 4 seconds or less (check warns otherwise).
- An actor must be inside the frame when it acts: pan or `follow` first.
- Put a prop where the hand will be when `hold` starts; walk the actor next to it first.
- Leave 0.5 s between big actions; a 30 s film is usually 15-30 timed lines.


========================================
FILE: docs/ACTIONS.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/ACTIONS.md
========================================

# ACTIONS.md: the CharAI action catalogue, moods, and writing a new action

An **action** (`2.0 Mia: bow()`) is a small file of key poses in body terms, so one file works on
a toddler, a fat man and a tall thin woman. CharAI adds smooth curves, trailing head and
arms, anticipation and settle, weight, mood, hand keep-out, planted feet and blending.

## 1. Catalogue

Built in (see `docs/AUTHORING.md` for arguments): body `walk`, `run`, `sneak`, `enter`, `jump`,
`turn`, `stand`, `idle`, `kneel`, `crouch`, `recoil`, `sit`, `peer`, `breathe`, `wobble`,
`fallsit`, `backstep`, `bounce`, `skid`; arms `wave`, `point`, `reach`, `cheer`, `hold`, `drop`,
`clench`, `pet`, `hesitate`, `tug`, `shield`, `laugh`; face `face`; look `look`, `nod`.

Action files in `actions/` (shared) and `films/<film>/actions/` (that film only, wins); a file
with a built-in name replaces the built-in. The reference files show each feature: `bow` (angles,
an argument), `clap` (landmarks, a loop), `stumble` (travel, feet), `getup` and `standup` (start
in a pose), `stepup` (a step, `y`), `lean` (a wall), `jumpjoy` (`air`), `skip`, `hi` (raw arm
angles, `turn`), `scratchhead` (`contact`). Start a new action by copying the closest one.

## 2. Moods

`Mia: mood(sad)` or `mood(name=angry, strength=1.5)` colours everything she does until the next
`mood` line: posture, head, arms, step length and tempo, arm swing, action speed, face. It
blends over 0.6 s; `strength` 0..2. Moods: `neutral`, `happy`, `sad`, `angry`, `scared`,
`tired`, `proud`, `shy`. `face(...)` still changes just the face. Set the mood before a walk:
its step length and tempo are fixed when it starts (the posture still changes).

## 3. Writing an action

One file per action, `actions/<name>.js` (or in a film's `actions/` folder). The name in the
file must match the file name.

```js
(function (g) { (g.CharActions = g.CharActions || {}).NAME = {
  channel: 'body', doc: 'one line for authors', args: { deep: 1 },
  keys: [
    { t: 0.4, lean: 30, head: 10 },
    { t: 1.0, hold: true },
  ] }; })(typeof self !== 'undefined' ? self : this);
```

**Options** (all optional except `keys`):

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel` | 'body' | 'body' moves the whole body; 'arms' is a gesture over whatever the body does |
| `doc`, `args` | | one line for authors; arguments with defaults (`{ deep: 1 }`; a key value may be `a => 30 * a.deep`) |
| `planted` | 'both' | body: feet that stay exactly where they are: 'both', 'near', 'far', 'none' ('none' when `travel`, `air` or `step` is set) |
| `end` | 'stand' | body only: after the last key, ease back to standing (in `back` s, 0.45), or finish in a pose that holds: 'sit', 'kneel', 'squat', 'lie'; 'hold' keeps the last key |
| `loop` | none | `true`: repeat all keys until the next body line (`end` is then ignored); `[from, to]`: repeat that stretch (args `times`, or `for` = seconds), then go on to `end` |
| `travel` | 0 | body: leg lengths moved over the action (negative = backwards), spread evenly if no key sets `x`. The camera follows only if the script says `cam: follow(...)` |
| `air`, `height` | none, 0.4 | body: airborne from `air[0]` to `air[1]` s on a parabola `height` leg lengths high, landing with a squash (unless a key just after sets `squash`) |
| `step` | none | body: a step `{ ahead, height }` in leg lengths in front; feet go onto it with `footNear: 'step'` |
| `wall` | none | a wall this many leg lengths ahead (negative = behind) for the `wall` landmarks |
| `contact` | false | `true`: the hands touch the head or body on purpose; the keep-out leaves them alone all through |
| `from` | | 'any': start from whatever pose the actor is in (else a sitting or lying actor stands first, unless the first key has a `pose`) |
| `anticipation`, `settle`, `overlap` | 1 | 0..2: the counter-move before the first key, the overshoot after the last, how much head and arms trail |
| `face` | none | a mood face while it plays (`happy`, `sad`, ...) |
| `hold`, `release` | 0, 0.35 | arms: seconds to hold the last key, seconds to ease back out (arms actions never use `end`) |

**Key fields.** `t` (seconds after the action starts, above 0, increasing) is required. Each
other field is its own smooth curve through the keys that set it; a field never set stays at
standing (or at the first key's `pose`). A key with only `t` and `hold: true` is a pause.

| Field | Channel | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pose` | body | 'stand', 'sit' (on the ground), 'kneel', 'squat', 'heels' (both knees down), 'lie' (on the back): a whole pose for this body; other fields in the key adjust it |
| `lean`, `bend` | both | upper body forward (+) or back (-); round (+) or arch (-) the back, degrees |
| `twist`, `tilt` | both / body | turn the chest; tip the hips, degrees |
| `head`, `neck` | both | chin down (+) / up (-); neck forward (+), degrees |
| `turn` | both | -1..1: the face turns toward (+) or away from (-) the camera (features squeeze and slide); a "no" = 0.5, -0.5, 0.5 |
| `crouch` | body | 0 standing .. 1 deep squat (knees bend, feet stay) |
| `y` | body | raise the pelvis by this many leg lengths (onto a step, a ledge; 0.25 = a stair) |
| `rise` | body | 0..1: up on the toes |
| `bob` | arms | lift (+) or drop (-) the whole body, head heights |
| `x` | body | pelvis forward from where THIS action started, leg lengths (not cumulative across actions) |
| `chest`, `squash` | body | torso stretch (1 normal, 0.9 squashed, 1.1 tall); whole body `[width, height]` |
| `handNear`, `handFar` | both | put that wrist at a **landmark** (below), solved for this body |
| `armNear`, `armFar` | both | raw angles `[shoulder, elbow, wrist]`: shoulder 0 hanging down, 90 forward, 180 up; elbow 0 straight .. 140 folded, bending the forearm forward and up; `[90, 90, 0]` puts the hand in front of the face on any body |
| `footNear`, `footFar` | body | `[ahead, lift, toe angle]` in leg lengths from where the pelvis started (standing: `[0.12, 0, 0]`, `[-0.08, 0, 0]`), or `'step'` / `['step', dx]`. A foot down in the same place at two keys is planted between them |
| `hands` | both | `'open'` or `{ near: 'open', far: 'fist' }`: relaxed, fist, open, point, grip, thumb (thumb up) |
| `mouth` | both | a mouth swap while this key plays (`'o'`, `'open'`, `'grit'`), `null` back to the mood |
| `hold`, `stand` | both / body | `true`: arrive and leave with zero speed; `true`: this key is the standing pose |

"Near" = the arm or foot on the camera side.

**Landmarks** for `handNear` / `handFar`: `'chin'`, `['chest', dx, dy]` or
`{ at: 'chest', dx: 0.3, dy: 0 }`, dx forward and dy up in head heights, measured on the actor
at that moment (after lean, crouch, posture and mood). A head is 1 head height tall, so
dy 0.1-0.3 is a small shift.

| Landmark | Where |
| --- | --- |
| `top`, `forehead`, `eye`, `mouth`, `chin`, `ear`, `backhead` | on the surface of the head (`ear` is over the ear, `backhead` behind the head) |
| `neck`, `chest`, `belly`, `hip`, `back`, `seat` | on the body (`hip` = hand on the hip, `seat` = behind the bottom) |
| `knee`, `ground` | in front of the near knee; on the ground half a leg length ahead |
| `front`, `up`, `out`, `down` | at full arm's length from that shoulder: straight ahead, straight up, up and forward, down. Use them for reaching; for a hand near the head use a head landmark with dx, dy |
| `wall`, `wallHigh`, `wallLow` | on the `wall` (option) at shoulder, head and hip height |

A hand sent to a landmark lands on it at that key on every body. If it is out of reach, the
body helps (the head nods toward a hand going to the head; the body leans and crouches toward
the ground), and what is still too far is reached as far as the arm goes. The keep-out (hands
out of the head, chest and belly) moves only hands that are not on a landmark and not in a
`contact: true` action.

**Details.**
- Raw arm angles are relative to the torso (a `lean` tips the arms with it); hand targets are not.
  Arms are also moved by the mood, belly clearance and keep-out (free hands only), small springs
  and a walking stick.
- Body-only: `chest`, `squash`, `crouch`, `rise`, `y`, `x`, `pose`, feet. Arms actions add `lean`,
  `bend`, `head`, `neck`, `twist`, `turn`, `bob` to the body.
- A wall landmark is reached only within arm's length: wall 0.5-0.9 leg lengths ahead.
- `loop: [a, b]` plays to b, repeats a..b, then plays on to the last key and `end`; `loop: true`
  does the same with `times=`/`for=`, else repeats until the next body line.
- Started while sitting or lying, an action without a starting `pose` plays only its upper body.
- Moods slow or speed actions and steps: sad 30%/22% slower, tired 35%/28%, shy 15%/10%;
  happy and angry about 10% quicker.
- `+0.2` in a script = 0.2 s after the same actor's previous line ends.
