- `check` calls a foot more than 6 px up outside a `jump` or `air` time "floats".

## 4. Worked examples

**Clap** (arms, landmarks, a repeating stretch):

```js
(function (g) { (g.CharActions = g.CharActions || {}).clap = {
  channel: 'arms', doc: 'clap (times = claps)', args: { times: 4, for: 0 }, loop: [0.3, 0.56], face: 'happy',
  keys: [
    { t: 0.3, handNear: ['chest', 0.35, 0.12], handFar: ['chest', 0.3, -0.08], hands: 'open' },
    { t: 0.43, handNear: ['chest', 0.32, 0.02], handFar: ['chest', 0.32, 0.0] },
    { t: 0.56, handNear: ['chest', 0.35, 0.12], handFar: ['chest', 0.3, -0.08] },
  ] }; })(typeof self !== 'undefined' ? self : this);
```

**Stand up from sitting** (start in a pose, pass through another, hand on the ground):

```js
(function (g) { (g.CharActions = g.CharActions || {}).standup = {
  channel: 'body', doc: 'stand up from sitting on the ground', planted: 'none', anticipation: 0,
  keys: [
    { t: 0.25, pose: 'sit', hold: true },
    { t: 0.7, pose: 'squat', lean: 34, handNear: 'ground', hands: 'open' },
    { t: 1.3, stand: true },
  ] }; })(typeof self !== 'undefined' ? self : this);
```

## 5. Rules of thumb

2-4 keys; 0.3 s between keys for a big move, 0.12 s for a hit; `hold: true` on the pose to read.

## 6. Check and look

`node tools/actioncheck.cjs actions/<name>.js` names each error and what to write.
`node tools/action.cjs <name> out.png --skin=tot,baker,vera` draws a strip; add `--mood=sad,angry`,
`--fixed` (a still camera, so travel shows), `--film=<film>` (that film's own actions), or a
sequence `"sit(); <name>()"`. A declared wall or step is drawn in grey. Test bodies: `tot`, `baker`,
`vera`, `gramps`, `titan`, `skye`, `captain` (walking stick), `duchess`.


========================================
FILE: docs/SPEECH.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/SPEECH.md
========================================

# SPEECH.md: CharAI faces and talking

Any actor can show feeling and speak a line from one script line. CharAI draws pictures
only; sound is added at render time (section 5).

## 1. Script calls

| Call | Channel | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `face(mood, strength=1)` | face | brows, lids, smile and the face swaps of a mood, blended over 0.35 s. Moods: neutral, happy, excited, sad, angry, scared, surprised, determined, tired, proud, shy. strength 0..2 |
| `mood(name, strength=1)` | mood | the body's mood (`docs/ACTIONS.md`); it also sets the face, unless a later `face` line changes it |
| `say("text", for=0, track="", words="", beats=0)` | say | speak a line. `for` = seconds (0 = estimated, about 4.5 syllables a second plus pauses). `beats=1` adds small beat gestures of the near hand on stressed syllables |

Speech runs beside everything else: an actor can walk, wave or sit while talking. A new `say`
cuts the previous one. Automatic life is always on: blinks (also on every face change), small
eye darts, a nod on each stressed syllable, a brow lift on emphasis (the last strong word before
`!`, or a word in CAPITALS).

```
0    cam: frame(on=Mia, top=head, bottom=chest, x=0.4, over=0)
0.2  Mia: face(happy)
0.4  Mia: say("Good morning, little one!", for=1.8)
+0.3 Mia: face(sad, strength=0.7)
+0   Mia: say("I lost my hat.")
```

## 2. Timing sources, best first

1. **A track**: `say("text", track="lines/hello.json")`, a file in the film folder. Either
   Rhubarb Lip Sync JSON (`{"mouthCues":[{"start":0,"end":0.1,"value":"X"}, ...]}`; values A-H
   and X) or a plain list `[{"t": 0.0, "v": "rest"}, {"t": 0.12, "v": "mbp"}, ...]` with the
   nine names below. Give `for` the length of the clip.
2. **Word timings**: `words="0:Good 0.32:morning 0.9:little 1.15:one"`, start time and word,
   separated by spaces. Each word's mouth shapes are spelled out inside its slot.
3. **Text only**: the engine spells out the mouth shapes (English rules: m, b, p close the
   lips; f, v show the teeth on the lip; o, oo, w round the lips; ee, i, s, t show the teeth;
   l lifts the tongue; vowels open; the stressed syllable of each word opens wider and longer;
   commas and full stops rest the mouth). Text in other scripts (no Latin letters) gets a
   language-neutral open-close rhythm, one opening per character. The mouth rests at the end.

**Getting timings from voice tools** (nothing is downloaded by the engine): Rhubarb Lip Sync
(`rhubarb -f json -o hello.json hello.wav`) gives a track directly; forced aligners (Montreal
Forced Aligner, Gentle, aeneas) and most text-to-speech services that return word or phoneme
times give word timings: write them as `words="t:word ..."`. Without audio, text only is fine.

## 3. Mouth shapes (visemes)

Nine shapes, by name: `rest` (closed, relaxed), `mbp` (lips pressed), `ah` (wide open), `ee`
(wide, teeth), `oh` (round, open), `oo` (small, pursed), `fv` (upper teeth on the lower lip),
`l` (open, tongue up), `wq` (rounded, small). A mouth blends into the next over 70 ms, and a
closed `mbp` is always reached.

## 4. What a skin needs

- **The mannequin's head** (a skin with `build` and no `swaps.mouth`) draws all nine shapes from
  numbers, and draws brows, lids and a smile-to-frown blend from the face parameters. Nothing
  to add.
- **A drawn head** gives `swaps.mouth` (see `docs/RIG.md`, "Face swaps"). Any of the nine names
  it lacks falls back to the nearest shape it has, scaled: `ah` -> `open`; `ee` -> `grit`, else
  `open` squashed; `oh` -> `o`, else `open` narrowed; `oo` and `wq` -> each other, `o` or a
  small `open`; `fv` -> `grit` squashed, else closed; `l` -> `open` squashed; `rest` and `mbp`
  -> `neutral` or `closed`. So a skin with just `open` and `closed` talks acceptably, and one
  with the seven mood mouths (neutral, smile, open, o, worried, grit, sad) talks well.
- **A beard or a mask**: any `parts.head` or `parts.hair` piece whose point box has bottom below
  0.12, top below 0.62, height at least 0.12 and centre below 0.32 drops with the jaw while
  speaking, so a bearded face talks through its beard even with its mouth hidden.
- **Brows and eyes of a drawn head**: the face picks `brow` and `eye` swaps by mood (up, down,
  worried; wide, narrow, sad, happy, closed) and lifts the brows on emphasis.

## 5. Check and render

```
node tools/say.cjs shapes.png --skin=mia --shapes                 # the nine mouths of a skin
node tools/say.cjs line.png --skin=mia --text="Good morning!" --for=1.5 --mood=happy,sad
node tools/say.cjs line.png --skin=mia --film=myfilm --track=lines/hello.json --text="Hello"
node tools/render.cjs films/<film> out.mp4 --fps=30 --audio=films/<film>/lines/all.wav
```

`--audio` muxes a sound file under the picture (ffmpeg); its time 0 is the film's time 0, so
place each line's `say` at the time the line starts in the sound file.

## 6. Rules of thumb

- Frame talking close-ups with `cam: frame(on=X, top=head, bottom=chest)`; the camera follows
  the head, so a stoop or a nod stays in frame.
- Give `for` from the real line when there is audio; without audio, leave it out.
- Put `face(...)` just before `say`, and change it between lines, not inside one.
- Keep lines under about 4 seconds; split long speeches into several `say` lines with `+0.2`.


========================================
FILE: docs/PAIRS.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/PAIRS.md
========================================

# PAIRS.md: CharAI actions for two

One script line drives two actors:

```
2.0  Kai: hug(with=Tot)
+0   Vera: give(with=Skye, prop=loaf)
```

Kai walks (or turns) to the right distance, Tot turns to face Kai, then both play their role from the
same moment on one clock. The line ends when both roles end and occupies both actors: a later `+0`
line of either one waits for it (`check --timeline` lists the line under both names), and an absolute
time inside it warns that it cuts the pair short.

## 1. The file

A paired action is one file in `actions/` (or a film's `actions/`), like a single action with two roles:

```js
(function (g) { (g.CharActions = g.CharActions || {}).hug = {
  pair: true, doc: 'arms round each other, a squeeze, let go', gap: 0,
  a: {                                     // the one the line names (Kai)
    low: { pose: 'heels', lean: 20 },      // when the partner is a child
    keys: [
      { t: 0.45, handNear: ['front', -0.15, 0.05], hands: 'open' },
      { t: 0.9, lean: 9, handNear: 'partner.around', handFar: ['partner.around', 0, 0.1] },
      { t: 1.25, lean: 14, chest: 0.96, handNear: 'partner.around', handFar: ['partner.around', 0, 0.1] },
      { t: 1.95, lean: 9, handNear: 'partner.around', handFar: ['partner.around', 0, 0.1] },
      { t: 2.45, pose: 'stand', hands: 'relaxed' },
    ] },
  b: { keys: [ ... ] },                    // the partner (Tot), same clock
}; })(typeof self !== 'undefined' ? self : this);
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pair: true` | this file is a pair |
| `doc` | one line |
| `gap` | the closest the two torsos come while a hand is on the partner, in arm lengths of the shorter arm: 0 a hug, 0.3 a shove, 0.5 a handshake or a hand-over, 0.7 a punch, 4 a throw |
| `args` | extra arguments both roles get, for example `{ prop: '' }` |
| `a`, `b` | the two roles. Each is an action as in `docs/ACTIONS.md`: `keys`, `planted`, `end`, `face`, `anticipation` and so on |

Everything in `docs/ACTIONS.md` works in a role. Write each role as if the partner stood in front,
facing you. Both roles share one clock: a key at 0.6 in `a` and a key at 0.6 in `b` happen together,
whatever the two bodies weigh or feel (moods still colour posture, not timing).

## 2. Hands on the partner

A hand target can be a place on the partner: `handNear: 'partner.back'`, or with an offset
`['partner.shoulder', 0, -0.4]` (forward, up, in your own head heights).

| Target | Where |
|---|---|
| `partner.head`, `partner.top`, `partner.face` | the head; the top of it (a pat on a child's head); the face |
| `partner.shoulder` | on top of the shoulder (offset down for the upper arm) |
| `partner.chest`, `partner.belly` | the front of the body |
| `partner.back`, `partner.waist` | the back at chest height; the lower back |
| `partner.side` | the flank, halfway through the body |
| `partner.around` | round the body at your own chest height, as far as your arm goes: the hug target |
| `partner.front` | the nearest point of the partner's front, body or knee: what a child can reach on a grown-up |
| `partner.hip`, `partner.knee` | |
| `partner.hand` | if the partner's key also says `partner.hand`, both hands meet halfway, at the shorter one's chest (a handshake; offsets raise it: a high five uses `['partner.hand', 0, 1.2]`). Otherwise the partner's hand as drawn (a block meets the fist) |
| `partner.arm` | the partner's forearm |

How it works: a key aims the arm at where the partner is expected; then, every frame, after both
bodies have breathed, swayed and taken their mood, the stage puts the hand exactly on the partner's
point as drawn. A hand stays on the partner from a key that names a place until the next key on that
hand that names something else, so two keys with the same target hold the contact between them.

## 3. Different sizes

The engine tells each role how the two compare:

- `low: { ... }` on a role: fields that replace those of every key (except `pose` and `stand` keys)
  when the partner is under 0.6 of your height (a grown-up with a child). Typical:
  `low: { pose: 'heels', lean: 20 }` (both knees down) or `low: { crouch: 0.4, lean: 20 }`.
- `high: { ... }` the same when the partner is over 1.65 of your height (a child with a grown-up),
  typically `high: { handNear: 'partner.front' }`.
- `low` and `high` inside one key replace that key's fields only and win over the role's.
  Put hand targets in key-level `low`/`high` (on the keys that touch), and posture in the role's.
- Keys may be functions of the arguments: `x: a => -0.3 * a.push`. A role gets `a.size` (partner
  height / yours), `a.push` (partner weight / yours, 0.2..5), `a.apart` (distance at the start, your
  head heights) and the line's own arguments.
- A taller body also leans down by itself when a key's target on the partner is out of reach.

Scale reactions with `push`: a shove moves the partner `-0.55 * s(a)` leg lengths where
`s = a => Math.max(0.35, Math.min(2.2, a.push))`. Keep the receiver still (`x: 0`) until the hit
lands, so the hit lands.

## 4. Placement, layering, contact

- A walks to the distance where the torsos come `gap` apart while touching, measured on the drawn
  bodies (a belly or an apron counts), then corrected: torsos never overlap, and a hand that falls
  short brings the two closer while there is room.
- While a hand is on the partner the two are drawn together: both far arms, then both bodies, then
  both near arms. An arm round a back goes behind the partner; the near arm lies over them.
- A gap of less than a leg length is closed with a quick step (`stepback`, forward or back) instead of
  a walk. After the release, if the two would stand closer than a third of an arm (or `gap`), A
  steps back, so two actors never rest inside each other.
- After a hit lets go, the partner may stagger or fall anywhere; their feet follow their own keys
  (`planted: 'none'` on a staggering role).
- A role that touches a partner under 0.6 of its height and has no `low` kneels on the heels; a
  role's lean is kept within 50 degrees forward, so reaching down never topples.
- A grown-up's arm round a child's back is drawn behind the child (it shows on the child's back,
  not across its face). A walking stick in a hand that touches the partner is tucked along the forearm.
- `cam: frame(on=A+B)` keeps both whole, heads, feet and hands, for any two sizes (`pad=` widens it).

## 5. Props in pairs

A key with `give: true` in role `a` and `take: true` in role `b` hands the line's `prop` over at those
moments. `release: true` and `catch: true` throw it: it flies on an arc from the hand to the catching
hands. See `docs/PROPS.md`.

## 6. The reference pairs and how long they take

Every pair takes `speed=` (2 = twice as fast) or `for=` (seconds for the action itself). A line lasts:
the walk-up (about 0.6 s for a step, a walk at the actor's pace, often 1-2 s, for more than a leg
length), plus the action below at speed 1, plus about 0.45 s to stand, plus 0.6 s if A steps back.

| Name | Gap | Action | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hug` | 0 | 2.5 s | arms round each other, a squeeze, let go; a grown-up kneels on the heels for a child |
| `handshake` | 0.55 | 2.0 s | hands meet halfway, three pumps |
| `highfive` | 0.6 | 1.3 s | hands raised, slapped above the shorter one's head |
| `pat` | 0.45 | 1.6 s | three pats on the shoulder; a child's head; a grown-up's knee from a child |
| `shove` | 0.3 | 1.6 s | two hands to the chest, the partner staggers back by weight |
| `punchblock` | 0.7 | 1.2 s | a play punch at the face, met by the forearm |
| `punchfall` | 0.65 | 1.3 s | a cartoon punch, the partner falls on the back and stays down |
| `give` | 0.5 | 1.3 s | hand over a prop: `give(with=B, prop=loaf)`; a giver not holding it picks it up first (+2-4 s) |
| `throwto` | 4 | 1.8 s | throw a prop, the partner catches it: `throwto(with=B, prop=ball)` |

A film that writes its own pairs (as `films/together/` does) times them the same way.

Not expressible yet: walking hand in hand, lifting and carrying a person (one body would have to move
the other's root), a chain of more than two.

## 7. Check and look

```
node tools/actioncheck.cjs actions/hug.js                 fields, partner targets, a toddler and an adult both ways
node tools/action.cjs hug out.png --skin=captain+tot,vera+skye     a strip per pair (with= is added)
node tools/action.cjs give out.png --skin=vera+skye --props=loaf --hold=loaf
```

Look at the strips: hands on the partner, no body through another, the smaller one not lost behind
the bigger, the reaction size fitting the weights.


========================================
FILE: docs/PROPS.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/PROPS.md
========================================

# PROPS.md: objects the CharAI actors use

A prop is one file in `extras/props/` (shared) or a film's `props/`, drawn in stage pixels at the usual
actor scale (a 7-head grown-up is about 420 px tall at `scale=60`). Copy `extras/props/box.js`.

## 1. The grip contract

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | as the file |
| grip | the point the hand closes on is the origin (0, 0) of the drawing; draw around it, y down |
| `base` | `[x, y]` of the point that rests on the ground |
| `size` | `[w, h]` px, for reach and layout |
| `weight` | 0 (a loaf, a ball) .. 1 (a door). Over 0 the holder leans back by `0.3 * weight` rad and the knees give |
| `grips` | optional `{ near: [x, y], far: [x, y] }`: where two hands go on a big object (a box) |
| `seat` | optional `[x, y]`: where a sitter's hips go (a chair; relative to the grip). The sitter faces +x, the chair back is on the left |
| `upright` | optional `true`: it stands on the ground and is walked up to, knocked on, leaned on (a door, a wall). Its face is x = 0 of the drawing |
| `hang` | true: hangs and swings from the hand (a lantern, a bag); false: turns with the hand |
| `glow` | optional light, as in `lantern.js` |
| `draw(t, ctx)` | SVG string; `ctx = { held, swing }`. A pure function of `t` |

The five reference props: `loaf` (one hand, 0.05), `ball` (one hand, 0.03, spins), `box` (two hands,
0.6), `chair` (a seat, 0.35), `door` (an upright, 1).

## 2. In the script

```
prop box at 900
prop chair at 1300
prop door at 1700
1.0  Kai: pickup(prop=box)        walks up, squats, takes it at the key that reaches the ground, holds it at the chest
+0.5 Kai: putdown()               bends down to the ground
+0   Kai: drop(quiet=1)           lets go there (drop() alone lets it fall from the hand)
+0   Kai: sit(on=chair)           walks to it, turns, sits with the hips over the seat at its height
+1   Kai: standup()
+0   Kai: knock(on=door)          stands at the action's wall distance from the door's face
```

- `prop=<name>` on an action whose file reaches the ground (or has a key with `grab: true`): the
  actor walks so the hand lands on the prop, and holds it from that key (`hold(prop, weight)`).
- `on=<seat prop>` with `sit`: the seat height comes from the prop (`base` minus `seat`).
- `on=<upright prop>` with an action that has `wall:` (knock, lean, push): the actor stands that many
  leg lengths from the prop's face.
- `give(with=B, prop=loaf)` and `throwto(with=B, prop=ball)` are paired actions (`docs/PAIRS.md`):
  the prop changes hands at the keys marked `give`/`take`, or flies on an arc between `release`
  and `catch`. A giver who does not hold the prop walks to it and picks it up first; the taker
  holds it from the moment of the handover (`hold(prop, quick=1)`), so it never jumps.
- A prop with `grips` (the box) is held with the near hand on `grips.near` and the far hand on
  `grips.far`.
- Pages made by `tools/check.cjs` always load `actions/stepback.js` and `actions/pickup.js`, which the
  stage adds itself; a page built by hand must load them too.
- A prop is found at its `at` place; a prop already moved by an earlier action is taken from where
  the script placed it, not where it was dropped (place it again with a new `prop` line if needed).

## 3. Check and look

```
node tools/action.cjs "pickup(prop=box)" out.png --skin=gramps,tot --props=box@900 --fixed
node tools/action.cjs "sit(on=chair)" out.png --skin=vera,tot --props=chair@900 --fixed
node tools/action.cjs throwto out.png --skin=vera+skye --props=ball --hold=ball --zoom=0.9 --at=900
```

Not yet: pushing or pulling a heavy object along the ground (the prop does not move with the push),
a chair that faces left, a prop taken back from wherever it was dropped (it is taken from its `at`).


========================================
FILE: docs/HOSTS.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/HOSTS.md
========================================

# Using CharAI from other tools and pages

CharAI draws characters only, on a transparent layer. The host supplies the scenery.

## Build

```
node tools/build.cjs        # dist/char.js (global Char) and dist/char.esm.js
```

Re-run it whenever `src/` changes. The bundle has no dependencies and loads in Node without a DOM.

## Web component

```html
<script src="dist/char.js"></script>
<char-stage width="1280" height="720" skins="skins/kai.js" actions="actions/hi.js" autoplay loop controls>
  <script type="text/plain">film "x" 4s
actor Kai = skin kai at 200
0 Kai: walk(to=900)</script>
</char-stage>
```

Attributes: `src` (film script URL, needs http, not file://; or inline script text), `skins`, `actions`
(space separated script URLs), `width`, `height`, `autoplay`, `loop`, `controls`.
Methods `seek(t)`, `play()`, `pause()`; properties `duration`, `currentTime`; events `ready`, `error`.
Put the page's ground line at the script's `ground=`. See `examples/page.html`.

## Page-owned clock

`Char.mount(el, { script, skins })` returns `{ duration, seek(t), destroy() }`. `seek` is a pure
function of t and may be called in any order. `examples/timeline.html` follows the film page
contract: `window.seek(t)`, `?static=1`, `?t=`. Load skin and action files before mounting.

## Transparent video

```
node tools/export.cjs films/bare-test out.webm --format=webm --fps=30   # VP9 with alpha
node tools/export.cjs films/bare-test out.mov  --format=mov            # ProRes 4444 with alpha
node tools/export.cjs films/bare-test frames   --format=png            # PNG sequence
```

Optional `--w --h --from --to`. Films with a `set` line draw their own scenery; use bare-stage films.
ffprobe shows a WebM as yuv420p: the alpha is stored separately (tag `alpha_mode=1`); decode it with
`-c:v libvpx-vp9`.

## Other hosts (untested snippets)

**Remotion** (untested): mount once, seek per frame.
```jsx
const ref = useRef(); const frame = useCurrentFrame(), { fps } = useVideoConfig();
useEffect(() => { ref.current.m ??= Char.mount(ref.current, { script, skins: CharSkins, width: 1280, height: 720 });
  ref.current.m.seek(frame / fps); });
return <div ref={ref} />;
```

**HyperFrames** (untested): register a seek on the composition timeline.
```js
const m = Char.mount(document.getElementById('chars'), { script, skins: CharSkins });
window.__timelines["main"].eventCallback?.("onUpdate", () => m.seek(tl.time()));
```

**GSAP** (untested): tween a number and seek on update.
```js
const o = { t: 0 };
gsap.to(o, { t: m.duration, duration: m.duration, ease: "none", onUpdate: () => m.seek(o.t) });
```

## Animated SVG

```
node tools/svgloop.cjs films/header out.svg --fps=10 --crop=0,360,1280,360 --round=24
```

Writes one SVG that plays a time range of a bare-stage film as a loop: real vector frames from the
engine, shown one at a time by a CSS animation. No script, no external file, so it also works in an
`<img>` tag on GitHub. Options: `--from --to --fps --crop=x,y,w,h --round --under --over --still
--decimals` (see the top of the tool). The motion stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`, showing the
`--still` frame. The frame at `--to` must equal the frame at `--from`, or the loop will jump. Each
frame stores the characters in full, so keep it short: the header, 7 s at 10 fps with two small
characters, is about 840 KB. `films/header` and `docs/img/src/` hold the header's film and artwork.


========================================
FILE: docs/VOICE-WINDOWS.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/VOICE-WINDOWS.md
========================================

# Voicing a CharAI film with Windows speech

No download needed: `tools/winvoice.cjs` uses the built-in Windows voices (David male,
Zira female) and turns their viseme events into an engine timing track.

1. Make one folder `films/<name>/lines/`.
2. For each line:
   `node tools/winvoice.cjs "Fresh bread!" films/<name>/lines/b1.wav --voice=David --rate=-1`
   It writes `b1.wav`, `b1.json` (the `{t, v}` track) and `b1.words.json` (word start
   times), and prints the duration in seconds. `--rate` is -10..10; slightly negative
   suits a heavy character, positive a quick one.
3. In `film.char`, give each line `say("text", for=<duration>, track="lines/b1.json")`.
   Add a matching `caption:` line with the same start time.
4. Retime: start each line when the previous one ended plus about 0.4 s, so nothing
   overlaps. Keep camera, face and gesture lines near their line.
5. Build one sound file, placing each wav at its start time (milliseconds in `adelay`):
   `ffmpeg -i b1.wav -i s1.wav -filter_complex "[0]adelay=1100:all=1[a];[1]adelay=4800:all=1[b];[a][b]amix=inputs=2:normalize=0,apad=whole_dur=21[o]" -map "[o]" all.wav`
   Set `apad` to the film length so audio and video end together.
6. `node tools/check.cjs films/<name>` then
   `node tools/render.cjs films/<name> films/<name>/film.mp4 --fps=24 --audio=films/<name>/lines/all.wav`
7. Check sync: `node tools/sheet.cjs films/<name> strip.png --n=12 --from=T0 --to=T1`
   around an m, b or p (lips must be closed in the frame at start time plus the track time).

Viseme mapping: silence rest; p,b,m mbp; f,v fv; l, th, t, d, n l; ah, aa, ae, aw, ay,
h, k, g ah; ao, ow, oy oh; eh, iy, ih, s, z ee; w, uw oo; er, r, sh, ch wq.

Notes: the track covers the whole clip, so `for` should equal the duration. Speech
pauses at commas can be long (about 0.5 s), which the mouth rests through.


========================================
FILE: docs/EVIDENCE.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/EVIDENCE.md
========================================

# CharAI evidence: what it costs to make characters, actions and films

This page reports what we measured, including where CharAI lost.

## How this was measured, and the limits

- Each case was run **once**. There are no repeats and no error bars.
- Token figures are the totals each AI agent run reported: all tokens, input and output together. They are not dollars.
- "Price-weighted" counts Claude Sonnet at half of Claude Opus, the ratio of their list prices. Figures are thousands of tokens.
- Times are agent working time.
- The engine agent's token counter reset once. Its per-round figures are therefore approximate, and one round is unmeasured.
- Picture quality was judged from still frames by the supervising model. Motion was judged from strips, not by watching. Lip sync was judged by the project owner by ear: it matches, but is not polished.
- "Lemo" below means the style-library workflow (Lemo-Opuscar, with crayon picture-book and silhouette styles). Its setup was not counted.

## 1. What a character costs

| | Skin file | Tokens | Time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before the mannequin: Kai, Opus | 16 KB | not separable from the episode | not separable |
| Before: Kai, Sonnet | 14 KB | not separable | not separable |
| Before: snow girl, Sonnet | 16.9 KB | not separable | not separable |
| After: 6 characters, Sonnet | 1.3 to 2.2 KB | about 41,800 each | about 40 s each |
| After: all 8 including the re-test pair | 1.3 to 2.2 KB | about 41,000 each | |

The agents worked from the documents without reading engine code. All eight pass the skin checker and run, jump and wave. Before the mannequin, character drawing was bundled with other work, so no per-character token figure exists.

![Skin file sizes](img/evidence-skin-size.svg)

## 2. What an action costs

36 actions were written by Claude Sonnet from `docs/ACTIONS.md` alone: about 8,200 tokens and 9 seconds each, 0.4 to 0.7 KB per action. All passed the action checker.

| Rating of the 36 | Good | Acceptable | Poor | Not viewed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First pass (agents' own verdicts) | 6 | about 14 | 7 | 9 |

Poor ones traced to engine gaps, such as no start state other than standing and no air time. One Claude Opus fix round (93,000 tokens, 12.2 minutes) followed. A Claude Sonnet review then repaired 28 actions (217,112 tokens, 4.8 minutes), rewriting 19. Verdicts after: 14 good, 14 acceptable, from the same agents. The log does not say how the other 8 were rated after the fix.

## 3. What a scene costs

All written by Claude Sonnet from the documents.

| Scene | Length | Script | Tokens | Minutes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Two characters, moods, 3 own actions | 20 s | 31 lines | 98,844 | 2.4 |
| Talking scene (includes face swaps for two characters) | 15 s | 35 lines | 105,351 | 3.1 |
| Talking scene with voice and sound | 21 s | not stated | 84,578 | 3.6 |
| Hug, handover, scuffle, 3 own paired actions | 20 s | 29 lines | 123,413 | 4.2 |
| Snow Day, scenery, character and acting | 14 s | 0.8 KB acting script | 320,890 | 15.4 |

The paired-action scene was judged weak as a whole, though hug and handover were readable. An Opus fix round followed (98,174 tokens, 11.5 minutes). Snow Day was a film made to match a reference picture, not shipped.

## 4. Against the style-library workflow

### Two 30-second episodes ("Kai")

| Method | Model | Ep 1 tokens | Ep 2 tokens | Both | Minutes | Price-weighted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lemo | Opus | 240,515 | 291,853 | 532,368 | 39 | 532 |
| Lemo | Sonnet | 340,175 | 327,027 | 667,202 | 74 | 334 |
| Engine | Opus | 255,604 | 221,729 | 477,333 | 33 | 477 |
| Engine | Sonnet | 203,205 | 221,852 | 425,057 | 25 | 213 |

On Opus, episode 1 cost the engine more tokens (255,604 against 240,515) and one more minute. It won on episode 2 and in total. Episode 2 reused Kai and the lamb in both methods.

New code written for episode 2:

| Run | Creature | Set | Animation | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lemo, Opus | 12,221 | 9,467 | 28,628 | 50,316 |
| Lemo, Sonnet | 12,281 | 9,698 | 29,109 | 51,088 |
| Engine, Opus | 16,955 | 16,277 | 2,349 script + 3,551 actions | 39,132 |
| Engine, Sonnet | 13,830 | 11,693 | 2,054 script + 4,264 actions | 31,841 |

The engine's creatures and sets were larger; its animation was much smaller.

![Animation code size](img/evidence-animation-size.svg)

### Silhouette film ("First Jump", 30 s, both on Opus)

| Measure | Lemo | Engine | Engine against Lemo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tokens | 318,987 | 391,611 | +23% |
| Minutes | 24.7 | 35.7 | +44% |
| Tool calls | 65 | 100 | +54% |
| Code, total | 45.2 KB | 35.6 KB | -21% |
| Figures | 13.9 KB | 4.0 KB | -71% |
| Animation | 27.6 KB | 7.8 KB | -72% |
| Sky, water, set | 2.4 KB (9 KB shader reused) | 11.0 KB | +358% |
| Engine changes | 0 | 12.8 KB | |
| Fix rounds | 6 | 5 | |
| Video file | 32.0 MB | 7.9 MB | -75% |

**CharAI lost this test on cost and on looks.** The other workflow's film looked better (richer sky, more varied shots, more natural child proportions) and cost less. The engine's film was clean and on the beat but flatter, with big-headed figures that merge. The project owner also judged the other workflow's motion better at that time.

Afterwards the engine gained motion clips, spring physics for hair, scarf and pack, soft limbs, moods, speech and two-character contact. **The silhouette comparison was not re-run.** We do not claim the gap has closed.

## 5. What the engine cost to build

This is a one-time cost, paid once and shared by every later film.

| Stage | Opus | Sonnet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Early engine (skeleton, skins, script language) | 875,467 | |
| Snow Day engine upgrade (motion clips, springs) | 446,931 | |
| Stages 0 to 1 (rig rules, mannequin, tools, proofs) | 176,755 | 662,235 |
| Stage 2 (pose language, moods, 44 actions) | 215,883 | 621,937 |
| Stage 3 (faces, speech, proof scene) | 108,591 | 118,018 |
| Windows voice tool and talking scene | | 84,578 |
| Packaging | | 90,929 |
| Stage 4 contact (round unmeasured, 44.5 min) | not measurable | 123,413 |
| Release preparation, stage 4 fix | 98,174 | 120,289 |

Final totals for the first-release build: Sonnet 1,821,399 tokens; Claude Opus at least 599,403 plus the unmeasured round. The first two rows are not in those totals. The Opus figures are differences of a counter that reset once.

**Break-even.** The log works it out only for the early engine (875,467 Opus tokens) against the two Kai episodes:

| Engine instead of Lemo | Saving per episode | Break-even |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opus instead of Opus | about 27,500 tokens | about 32 episodes |
| Sonnet instead of Opus | about 160 price-weighted thousand | about 6 episodes |
| Sonnet instead of Sonnet | about 60 price-weighted thousand | about 15 episodes |

These break-evens cover the early engine only. The later stages added far more build cost and the log gives no break-even for them. The silhouette test saved nothing.

## 6. What has not been measured

- A film that reuses existing characters with nothing new to draw. This is the engine's best case, and it was never run.
- Anything longer than 30 seconds.
- Quality rated by humans.
- The host snippets for Remotion, HyperFrames and GSAP, and the `src` attribute over http.
- Dollar cost: input and output tokens were not reported separately.


========================================
FILE: docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md
========================================

# CharAI: known issues

What is known to be wrong, missing or untested in the first release. Agents wrote all of the
code; no person has reviewed it line by line yet.

## Not in this release

- **Views.** Side view only. No three-quarter or front view, so arms cannot cross in depth and
  elbows cannot point out sideways.
- **Two-character actions not built:** walking hand in hand, lifting and carrying a child,
  pushing or pulling a heavy object, and chains of more than two characters.
- **One airborne phase per action.** A double hop needs two actions.

## Faults you may see

- **Hug with a small child.** A grown-up's arm is drawn behind the child but still passes the
  back of its head. A toddler's arms are too short to go round a large belly, so its hands
  rest on the front.
- **Very different sizes.** A toddler's punch can fall short of a grown-up's knee. A very fat,
  short-armed character reaches a toddler only by kneeling on the heels.
- **Handover.** The two hands meet slightly off the object. An object is taken from where the
  script placed it, not from where it was last dropped.
- **Long garments.** A standing ankle-length skirt follows the legs too closely. A large belly
  overlaps raised thighs.
- **Speech.** Lip sync matches the words but is not polished: mouths are small in side view,
  head nods are guessed from the text and not taken from the audio, and the mouth rests for
  about half a second at commas. A beard hides most mouth movement.
- **Foot slides.** The film checker warns of planted feet sliding 3 to 12 px for a single
  frame in several example films. These are warnings, not errors.
- **Paired actions are long.** With the walk-up they take 3 to 5 seconds. The table in
  `PAIRS.md` gives each length; use `speed=` or `for=` to change it.

## Untested

- The Remotion, HyperFrames and GSAP snippets in `HOSTS.md`.
- `<char-stage>` inside a real host application, and its `src` attribute over http.
- Any system other than Windows, and any Node version other than the one used to build it
  (Node 18 or newer is assumed).
- `tools/winvoice.cjs` works on Windows only, because it uses Windows speech.
- Films longer than 30 seconds.

## Documents longer than intended

`ACTIONS.md` and `PAIRS.md` are longer than their targets (about 1,900 and 1,550 words), which
costs an agent more tokens to read.


========================================
FILE: examples/README.md
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/examples/README.md
========================================

# Examples: one `.char` file, one film

Each file is a complete short film that runs with the shared library plus `examples/skins/` and
`examples/actions/`. Run any of them from the engine folder:

```
node tools/check.cjs examples/hello.char                  # checks it, writes examples/hello.html (open to play)
node tools/render.cjs examples/hello.char hello.mp4       # 1280x720 MP4 (needs ffmpeg and Chrome or Edge)
node tools/sheet.cjs examples/hello.char sheet.png --n=8  # a contact sheet of 8 frames
```

| File | Shows | Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hello.char` | the smallest film: walk in, wave, a speech bubble | 8 s |
| `walk-run-jump.char` | walk, run, jump, skid; camera `cut`, `follow`, `zoom`, `pan` | 13 s |
| `moods.char` | the same walk under four `mood` lines | 14 s |
| `conversation.char` | `say` plus captions with `by=`, `look`, `face` | 13 s |
| `hug-and-handover.char` | paired actions `hug` and `give` with a prop | 15 s |
| `montage.char` | fifteen catalogue actions on five actors | 14 s |
| `local-action.char` | an action file next to the film: `actions/jig.js` | 9 s |

## The language in one page

```
film "Hello" 8s                  # header: title and length (first line)
set hillside                     # scenery (or: stage width=2400 ground=600 scale=68 for a bare stage)
actor Tess = skin tess at 640    # who, drawn by which skin, standing where (x in pixels or an anchor)
puppet Pip = bird at branch      # an animal; prop lantern at 532 adds an object

0.0  Tess: enter(from=left)      # a timed line:  <time> <target>: call(args), call(args)
+0.2 Tess: wave()                # +n = n seconds after Tess's previous line has finished
4.1  caption: "Hello!", by=Tess  # targets: an actor, a puppet, cam, caption, card, wind
```

- **Calls on one line start together**, so they must use different channels. Actors have
  `body` (walk, run, jump, idle, bow...), `arms` (wave, point, hold...), `face`, `mood`, `look` and `say`.
- **Body moves chain** with `+0`; a body line that starts too early cuts the previous one short.
- **The camera** (`cam`) has `pan`, `follow`, `cut`, `zoom`, `shake`, `fade` and `frame`/`home`.
- **Pairs**: `Kai: hug(with=Tot)` drives both actors. Actions are files in `actions/`.
- `#` starts a comment. Names are case-sensitive.

Full reference: [docs/AUTHORING.md](../docs/AUTHORING.md), with [docs/ACTIONS.md](../docs/ACTIONS.md),
[docs/SPEECH.md](../docs/SPEECH.md) and [docs/PAIRS.md](../docs/PAIRS.md).

## Colours in VS Code

1. Copy `editors/char.tmLanguage.json` into a folder `char-syntax/syntaxes/` with a `package.json` that
   declares a language `char` (extension `.char`) and a grammar for `source.char` pointing at it.
2. Put that folder in `~/.vscode/extensions/` and restart VS Code.


========================================
FILE: examples/hello.char
URL: https://github.com/riponcm/CharAI/blob/main/examples/hello.char
========================================

# hello.char - the smallest film: one actor walks in, waves and says hello.
# Run it:  node tools/check.cjs examples/hello.char     (then open examples/hello.html)
# More:    node tools/render.cjs examples/hello.char hello.mp4

# header: the title and length, a scenery set, and the cast
film "Hello" 8s
set hillside
actor Tess = skin tess at 640

# a timed line is  <seconds> <who>: action(args)
# enter() walks Tess in from off screen to her "at" place (700)
0.0  Tess: enter(from=left, speed=2), face(happy)

# +0.2 means "0.2 s after Tess's previous line has finished"; the caption has its own absolute time
+0.2 Tess: wave()
4.1  caption: "Hello!", by=Tess, for=1.8

# a card fades a title over the whole frame at the end
6.0  card: "The End"
